The resulting Landau-Zener probabilities have the same local lattice form as in the double-well problem, allowing the application of the QKNH theorem.
authors: Peter Stabel, James R. Anglin

papers.title: Painlev\'e transcendents in the defocusing Hirota equation with non-zero boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for the defocusing Hirota equation with non-zero boundary conditions \begin{align*} &iq_t+ q_{xx}-2\left(|q|^2-1\right)q +i\left(q_{xxx}-6|q|^2q_x\right)=0,\\ &q(x,0)=q_0(x)\to\pm 1, \quad x\to\pm\infty, \end{align*} which can be characterized using a Riemann-Hilbert problem through the inverse scattering transform. With the $\bar{\partial}$-steepest descent method and double scaling limit technique, we derive the long-time asymptotics of the solution in two transition regions \begin{align*} \mathcal{P}_{a} :=\left\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{+}: \left| {x}/{t}-a\right|t^{2/3}<C\right\}, \quad a\in\{-4,-8\}, \end{align*} where $C>0$ is a constant. It is shown that the asymptotic expansions in two transition regions can be expressed in terms of the Hastings--McLeod solution of the Painlev\'e II equation in the generic case and Ablowitz--Segur solutions in the non-generic case.
authors: Shuning Lin, Engui Fan

papers.title: Variational integrators for time-dependent Lagrangian systems on Lie groups
papers.abstract: We develop fixed-step variational integrators for time-dependent Lagrangian systems on Lie groups, derive their reduced dynamics, and analyze their long-time behavior by backward error analysis. We derive the continuous Euler-Lagrange equations, energy balance, and Noether conservation laws, and construct time-indexed discrete Lagrangians using retractions, with the midpoint-Cayley scheme treated explicitly. On their regularity domains, the resulting phase-space maps are symplectic. For left-invariant discrete Lagrangians, they reduce to Lie-Poisson maps that preserve coadjoint orbits and, when $G$ is connected, every Casimir function. A variational error analysis establishes second-order accuracy of the midpoint-Cayley method. We also construct an exactly symplectic, projectable extension on $T^*(\mathbb R\times G)$ whose formal modified Hamiltonian is affine in the momentum conjugate to time and admits symmetry reduction. Under uniform analyticity, coefficient bounds, and domain-containment assumptions, optimal truncation yields exponentially accurate interpolation and near-conservation of the modified extended Hamiltonian over exponentially long intervals. For a connected attitude network on $SO(3)^N$ with damping and uniformly positive, non-increasing coupling weights, we prove local asymptotic stability of the static consensus set for the continuous dynamics and exact preservation of total spatial momentum by the discrete scheme. Numerical experiments on the network and on a time-dependent rigid body on $SO(3)$ illustrate second-order convergence and the extended energy balance.
authors: Leonardo Colombo, Mar\'ia Emma Eyrea Iraz\'u, David Mart\'in de Diego, Mar\'ia Daniela S\'anchez, Marcela Zuccalli

papers.title: Symmetry-resolved spectroscopy of truncation-induced perturbations in loop tensor network renormalization of the six-vertex model
papers.abstract: Tensor network renormalization at finite bond dimension $\chi$ introduces truncation errors that are amplified by the renormalization-group (RG) flow. For loop tensor network renormalization (LoopTNR) on the $c=1$ critical line of the six-vertex model, with Luttinger parameter $K$, we identify these errors operator by operator from symmetry-resolved transfer-matrix spectra and conformal perturbation theory. With $O(2)$ symmetry imposed, the dominant error is the dimerization operator, which is allowed because LoopTNR breaks one-site translation. With less symmetry it is the $U(1)$ current or a charge-two vertex operator. The growth of the dimerization per RG step and a parameter-free ratio of its amplitudes agree with conformal perturbation theory to within a few percent. The parameter $K$ drifts slowly, owing to a weak marginal error and to the running induced by the dimerization. A larger $\chi$ lowers the initial amplitude of the error for $0.75\le K\le 1.5$ but changes neither the operator nor its growth rate.
authors: Akira Otsuki, Yuta Yamamoto, Kokin Cho, Rikuto Fushio, Masahito Yamazaki

papers.title: Generation of coherent-state Schr\"{o}dinger cat states in a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model implemented with Josephson junctions
papers.abstract: We investigate the generation of coherent-state Schr\"{o}dinger cat states using a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model (JCM) implemented in a Josephson-junction quantum circuit. We consider a specific superconducting flux-qubit implementation and estimate the resulting two-photon coupling constant. We numerically examine three types of noise: magnetic flux noise with $1/f$ fluctuations, energy relaxation associated with the flux-qubit $T_{1}$ decay, and photon loss in the bosonic mode obtained by quantizing the phase variable of the dc SQUID used for qubit readout. We find that photon loss has a particularly significant effect on cat-state fidelity. We also investigate the time evolution of the probability-amplitude distribution in the Pegg-Barnett phase-state basis for the $l$-photon JCM ($l=1,2,3,4$), starting from a coherent bosonic state. Finally, we assume that the bosonic mode is initially prepared in a displaced thermal state and then decoupled from the heat bath. We study the subsequent unitary evolution to determine how the initial temperature affects the fidelity and Wigner function of the generated cat states.
authors: Hiroo Azuma, William J. Munro, Kae Nemoto

papers.title: Curvature-Calibrated Friction and an Exact Gauge Symmetry for Quantum Hamiltonian Descent
papers.abstract: A design problem constrained by a partial differential equation can be solved coherently on a quantum computer. The objective is block-encoded rather than measured, and Quantum Hamiltonian Descent consumes it directly. We identify two obstacles in this pipeline and repair both. First, the oracle construction assumes affine generators with positive semidefinite Hermitian parts, which covariance entries violate for every off-diagonal generator. Encoding the covariance as an affine combination of positive semidefinite atoms restores both conditions at every register point, at the price of a representational floor, median 45% of the fitted family's own objective range for a fixed rank-three dictionary and 22% with a variable diagonal. Second, adding a constant to the objective leaves the measurement distribution exactly invariant, yet the mean-objective friction heuristic in current use assigns such objectives different schedules. Calibrating the friction to the landscape curvature restores the symmetry, though not the constant in $\nu = c\sqrt{\mu}$, and a bracketed sweep at matched objective-phase exposure, not end-to-end cost, places the best tested friction between 0.032 and 0.25 of critical damping on a diffusion-design benchmark, a broad plateau an order of magnitude below the classical default.
authors: Kentaro Hoshisashi

papers.title: Semiclassical Averaging and Temporal Fluctuations of Quantum Dark Solitons in the Lieb-Liniger Model
papers.abstract: We study the time evolution of quantum dark-soliton states of the Lieb--Liniger model, introduced by Sato--Kanamoto--Kaminishi--Deguchi as equal-weight superpositions of one-hole yrast states, and their relation to Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) solitons. We consider a simultaneous weak-coupling and large-system limit in which the repulsive coupling constant $c$ tends to zero and the particle number $N$ and ring circumference $L$ tend to infinity, with the mean density $\bar n=N/L$ and scaled circumference $\Lambda=L\sqrt{c\bar n}$ fixed. We conjecture that, in this limit, the normalized quantum density and its evolution at fixed scaled time $\tau=c\bar n t$ are described by a canonical-momentum average of normalized periodic one-soliton GP densities, each evolving at its own velocity. We explicitly parametrize the GP family by canonical momentum and provide numerical evidence for this correspondence. The different velocities explain the spreading of the averaged density notch despite shape preservation by individual solitons. In the infinite-line limit, we derive an analytic expression for the initial averaged profile, establish an inverse-fifth-power decay of its density deficit with distance from the soliton center, and express the Fourier transform of its deviation from the background as a series of Bickley--Naylor functions $\operatorname{Ki}_3$. Following the spreading of the initial notch, we investigate temporal density fluctuations of the quantum dark solitons and propose a relation between long-time mode variances and second moments of GP Fourier coefficients, supported by numerical comparisons of individual mode variances and the total variance. Yrast transition frequencies distinguish the initial dephasing time scale from the longer scale associated with finite-time averaging of fluctuations.
authors: Kota Kaneko, Kohei Motegi, Jun Sato

papers.title: Compiling Constraints into Neuromorphic Ising Machines
papers.abstract: Most practical combinatorial optimization problems involve constraints, and an Ising machine that flips one spin at a time can respect them only through energy penalties that raise barriers between feasible solutions. Here we show that a higher-order neuromorphic Ising machine can enforce constraints through programmable transitions rather than penalties. In an autoencoder-like architecture, each inner-layer neuron represents a move, a family of multi-spin transitions that maps every feasible state to another feasible state, receives the energy change of its move through connections that outer-layer neurons multiplicatively switch on or off, and updates the state through the same connections. A compiler turns constraints into this wiring with a number of auxiliary clauses that grows only polynomially for parity, cardinality, one-hot, partition and permutation constraints. Restricting the search to feasible states reduces constraint handling to move design, and we show that the fastest-annealing moves are not those that mix fastest but those that lower the deepest energy barriers, and that moves chosen from the objective lower them further than random ones. On third-order graph matching, the machine needs orders of magnitude fewer iterations than penalty-based neuromorphic machines. Configured as a sampler on a field-programmable gate array, it decodes the surface code with maximum-likelihood accuracy up to code distance 15 within 52 $\mu$s per shot and, under noisy syndrome measurements, decodes in real time for millisecond measurement rounds up to distance 9 with fewer logical errors than belief-propagation decoders.
authors: Faiek Ahsan, Shantanu Chakrabartty

papers.title: Dynamical edge universality and the Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble
papers.abstract: We prove dynamical edge universality for three families of interacting particle systems for every $\beta>0$: $\beta$-Dyson Brownian motion with an analytic potential, weighted $\beta$-corners processes, and a class of discrete-time Markov chains. Our results apply to general non-equilibrium initial data and show that the Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble emerges at positive times whenever the limiting density has a regular square-root edge. More precisely, after centering at the moving deterministic edge and rescaling space and time on the $n^{-2/3}$ and $n^{-1/3}$ scales, respectively, the trajectories of the top $k$ particles converge jointly in distribution to the top $k$ curves of the Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble, for every fixed $k$, in the topology of uniform convergence on compact time intervals. The proof combines dynamical loop equations with characteristic-flow estimates to establish local laws near the moving edge and upper bounds on the extremal particle. We then identify the stochastic evolution of every subsequential limit of the rescaled Stieltjes transform and establish convergence through the pole-evolution characterization of the Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble.
authors: Jiaoyang Huang, Shengjing Xu, Yulei Xu

papers.title: Ising-Encoded Computational Homogenization: Stress as a Quantum Observable
papers.abstract: Computational homogenization requires repeated solutions of representative volume element (RVE) problems to determine the effective response transferred to the macroscale, including the homogenized stress. Here, we develop a basis-encoded, energy-based variational quantum formulation for linear-elastic computational homogenization. The reduced finite-element energy of the RVE is expressed as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem and mapped to an Ising Hamiltonian, whose ground state represents the equilibrium fluctuation field on the encoding grid. Using the Hellmann--Feynman theorem, differentiation of the strain-dependent Hamiltonian with respect to the prescribed macroscopic strain yields stress observables whose expectation values recover the conventional volume-averaged homogenized stress. A key structural result is that, although the equilibrium Hamiltonian is two-local, the stress observables are one-local. In linear elasticity, the two-qubit coupling coefficients are independent of macroscopic strain, hence, differentiation eliminates all two-qubit coupling terms, leaving only identity and single-qubit Pauli-$Z$ operators. These observables are diagonal in the same computational basis as the Ising Hamiltonian and can therefore be evaluated from the same computational-basis measurements used for the energy. Consequently, the homogenized stress can be obtained directly from the optimized quantum state using the same computational basis measurements as the Ising Hamiltonian, without requiring reconstruction of the microscopic displacement field or an additional measurement basis. Ground states are approximated using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE), and the formulation is demonstrated on a two-dimensional periodic RVE.
authors: Mourad Halla, Suvranu De

papers.title: Counterfactual attribution of surface-code failures under non-Pauli noise: dependence on trajectory pairing
papers.abstract: Under Pauli noise in a stabilizer memory, attributing a quantum error-correction failure to the noise that caused it has a canonical answer; under non-Pauli noise the attribution depends on how trajectories are paired with their counterfactuals. We define a failing shot's cause set, the sites whose removal alone removes the failure, and separate it from pairing-independent net effects. The pairing enters wherever a fixed random draw meets a Born probability; making it maximal at every random step selects shared random numbers, while continuity does not. In a distance-three surface code, exact non-Pauli noise and its Pauli twirl fail at rates equivalent within a registered margin, yet under shared draws 20.2% of exact-noise failures need three or more sites, against 2.3% under the twirl. Other admissible pairings move the mean coherent cause count from 1.61 to 80 times the minimum the marginals allow, yet pairing-independent quantities barely separate the two models. Shot-level attributions should therefore state their pairing and report pairing-independent effects alongside.
authors: Kisung Jin, Gyuil Cha

papers.title: Interfacing Silicon Nitride Nanophotonics with Cuprous Oxide Rydberg Excitons
papers.abstract: Rydberg excitons in cuprous oxide (Cu$_2$O), the solid-state counterpart of Rydberg atoms, are hydrogen-like electron--hole quasi-particles with micron-sized wavefunctions and strong long-range interactions that promise optical nonlinearities at the few-photon level. Exploiting them in a waveguide quantum electrodynamics (WQED) setting can enable what atomic Rydberg platforms achieve only with ultrahigh vacuum and laser cooling/trapping---a guided optical mode interfaced with the Rydberg medium---while adding the scalability and advanced fabrication of integrated photonics. Here we demonstrate a monolithic, CMOS-compatible interface of Cu$_2$O Rydberg excitons with a SiN$_x$ nanophotonic waveguide. Under non-resonant excitation, excitonic emission from the Cu$_2$O microcrystal is coupled to the guided mode, routed along the waveguide, and collected from an output grating. The spectrum shows the phonon-assisted 1$s$ orthoexciton emission together with the low-lying 2$p$ and 3$p$ lines of the yellow Rydberg series. Spatially selective excitation excludes substrate background and direct scatter, and the enhanced linear polarization of the grating-collected signal identifies the TE-like guided mode as the collection channel. These results establish the complete material--device--measurement stack for a novel platform of nonlinear quantum nanophotonics based on Rydberg excitons.
authors: Artem Kryvobok, Hamza Ather, Julio Herreros Garc\'ia, Ziqi Niu, Abhishek Bharatbhai Solanki, Vahagn Mkhitaryan, Benjamin Cerjan, Alexandra Boltasseva, Vladimir M. Shalaev, Hadiseh Alaeian

papers.title: A Fa\`a di Bruno Convolution Identity in Parafermion Operator Products
papers.abstract: We give a detailed combinatorial proof of a Fa\`a di Bruno convolution identity used in parafermion operator-product calculations. The identity establishes the cancellation of potentially more singular terms and shows that the leading contribution combines the polynomial indices additively. The proof, originating in the author's doctoral thesis, provides a general derivation of an identity stated in earlier parafermion literature.
authors: Sam Kault

papers.title: Upper Bounds on the Radion Mass in a Warped Extra Dimension
papers.abstract:
We study absolute upper bounds on the mass ratio $R_{11}=m_{r_1}/m_{h_1}$ between the radion ($r_1$) and graviton ($h_1$) lightest modes in five dimensional warped models. We consider warped models with an admissible singular behavior in the infrared: i.e.~models with power-like ($\sim  ar\phi^{2n}$) and with exponential ($\sim e^{2
u ar\phi}$) bulk potentials, where $ ar\phi$ is the stabilizing bulk field. We find a correlation between $R_{11}$ and the singular behavior of the Ricci scalar, which allows to establish an absolute upper bound on the former. For the power-like models, the maximum value of $R_{11}$ increases with $n$. In the limit $n	o\infty$, the power-like model reproduces the exponential model and reaches the same upper bound as the latter. For the exponential model, we derive analytically the bound $R_{11}<1$, with the largest value approached for the case $
u	o 1^+$ (where $
u=1$ corresponds to the linear dilaton model) and consistent with unitarity sum rules. For exponential models we also obtain the absolute upper bound on the second radion mode ratio $R_{21}=m_{r_2}/m_{h_1}\lesssim 1.374$. This value is reached for $
u=2$ when the IR brane approaches the singularity. For this configuration, we verify that the scalar contribution satisfies the unitarity sum rule when the complete radion Kaluza-Klein tower is included.
authors: Leandro Da Rold, Eugenio Megias, Mariano Quiros, Lindber Salas

papers.title: Dynamical Variational Theory of Stochastic Reaction Networks
papers.abstract: Discrete stochastic population dynamics describe systems ranging from biochemical reaction networks and gene regulation to epidemic spreading, ecology, and population genetics, where finite populations generate strong intrinsic fluctuations. Predicting their dynamics, including mean populations, fluctuations, time-lagged correlations, response functions, and steady states, remains challenging: the chemical master equation admits no general analytical solution, numerical solutions scale poorly with system size, and standard approximations fail at low copy numbers. Using a field-theoretic representation of the reaction dynamics, we develop a dynamical variational approximation for stochastic reaction networks based on the Plefka expansion from spin-glass physics. For reaction systems with general stoichiometry and time-dependent rates, the expansion yields tractable non-Markovian effective dynamics with self-consistent memory. We further introduce a generalized self-consistent bubble resummation that provides closed predictions for means, correlations, and response functions. The formulation applies broadly to discrete stochastic population dynamics on networks, and we provide a numerical implementation with adaptive time stepping for user-defined systems. We benchmark the method on stochastic gene regulation, enzyme kinetics, and infection dynamics, where it accurately captures both time-dependent behaviour and steady states, including fluctuation-driven effects missed by conventional approximations. Together, these results establish a general analytical framework for stochastic reaction dynamics across transient and stationary regimes in strongly fluctuating low-copy-number systems.
authors: Moshir Harsh, Peter Sollich

papers.title: Convex splitting by binary quantum hypothesis testing
papers.abstract: How many independent quantum systems does it take to hide one system that is correlated with a reference? An observer can measure all the systems together with the reference to detect the correlation. We turn any such measurement into binary tests on a single system and the reference. For each test we bound the probability of declaring a signal when an independent pair was prepared. Averaging the largest signal acceptance probabilities allowed by these bounds controls the normalized trace distance in the convex-split lemma. A second bound gives a sufficient number of systems by minimizing the hypothesis-testing relative entropy over the state of the reference. Both bounds hold for density operators on separable Hilbert spaces. Comparing two distributions for the location of the hidden system gives one-shot bounds for private communication and one-way secret key distillation, including the public information available to an eavesdropper. For a fixed finite-alphabet model with separable quantum outputs and positive information advantage and variances, we recover the known Gaussian corrections to the attainable number of private or key bits from $n$ independent repetitions and bound the remaining loss by $\log_2 n+O(1)$ at fixed errors. The position-based key distillation protocol attains this bound with $O(n)$ public bits.
authors: Mark M. Wilde

papers.title: Remote Use of Quantum Machines in the Adversarial Scenario
papers.abstract: Networked quantum technologies allow users to operate quantum machines hosted by remote servers, but classical commands alone cannot ensure that only the intended user can prepare the useful inputs that activate them. We formulate the problem of adversarial remote use of quantum machines in the framework of quantum resource theories. A device controlled by Bob is correlated to a remote user, Alice, through a bipartite state, and also to an adversary Eve holding its purification. Alice and Eve compete to programme Bob's machine by remotely preparing its inputs: the conditional state carries the quantum resource, while the measurement outcome selects the machine operation. Remote use is truly advantageous when Alice is guaranteed to unlock a larger average task value than the adversary Eve, given the same marginal state of Bob. We show that for tasks with a convex figure of merit, the competition is governed by complementary upper roofs and, for spectral tasks, where the figure of merit is invariant under unitary operations, by a corresponding entanglement imbalance. Purification, work extraction, quantum batteries, and coherence distillation show that the same noisy state may secure exclusivity one machine but not another. Finally, we order Alice's and Eve's complete programming powers through a task-independent simulation preorder, based on the ensembles each party can prepare on Bob's side. Shared quantum correlations thereby become a key resource for controlling access to remote quantum machines.
authors: Mir Alimuddin, Leonardo Zambrano, Antonio Ac\'in

papers.title: Pairwise fermionic mode correlations in electric and magnetic backgrounds: Landau-level structure and Schwinger production
papers.abstract: We investigate mutual information and logarithmic negativity in fermionic Schwinger pair production in parallel electric and magnetic fields. Using spin-dependent Bogoliubov transformations, we construct the in-vacuum and derive the particle--antiparticle correlations for selected Landau modes. We also consider an initially entangled two-particle state and evaluate the correlations for six bipartitions. The physical Landau-level structure is treated explicitly by distinguishing modes with the same oscillator index from the spin representatives of a common physical Landau level. For matched higher levels, the pairwise redistribution relations retain the electric-only form, with the magnetic-field dependence entering through the Landau-level pair-production probabilities. When the two particle groups occupy different physical levels, the cross particle--antiparticle correlations become unequal, and we derive analytic relations characterizing this asymmetry. We further obtain the local logarithmic negativity from the ordinary partial transpose in a fixed occupation-space basis. Finally, we extend the analysis to a Sauter-type electric field in a constant magnetic background and examine the dependence of the pairwise correlations on the field parameters and Landau-level structure.
authors: Sahil Chetan Patnekar, Sristi Sanjivanee Goswami, Sanjay Pant, Shagun Kaushal

papers.title: The computational complexity of bosonic Lindbladian fixed points
papers.abstract: We study the computational complexity of estimating observables and sampling from stationary states, or fixed points, of bosonic Lindbladian dynamics with bounded-degree polynomial interactions. While the complexity of transient bosonic dynamics has been investigated, understanding the computational power of bosonic fixed points requires addressing subtleties of infinite-dimensional systems, including the existence, uniqueness, and convergence of stationary states. We establish a broad complexity landscape spanning universal quantum computation, efficient classical simulation, sampling hardness, and undecidability. First, we show that universal quantum computation can be embedded into observable estimation at the unique fixed point of a bosonic Lindbladian with a Hamiltonian of degree at most twelve and only linear photon loss. Moreover, this fixed point can be prepared from vacuum in polynomial time. On the classical side, we identify Gaussian regimes with incoherent pumping that admit efficient photon-number sampling and establish stability of classical approximability under sufficiently weak non-Gaussian Kerr perturbations. Conversely, for Gaussian fixed points without incoherent pumping, we establish hardness of exact sampling under constant-rate linear loss and hardness of approximate sampling at inverse-polynomial loss rates under standard boson-sampling conjectures. We also relate sampling from non-Gaussian fixed points to variants of boson sampling. Finally, we prove that deciding the existence of a stationary density operator is $\mathsf{RE}$-hard, even for purely dissipative Lindbladians with degree-five jump operators acting on at most four modes.
authors: En-Jui Kuo, Arsalan Motamedi, Mohammad Hafezi, Saeed Mehraban

papers.title: Momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo for twisted bilayer graphene: Interaction effects in the presence of remote bands
papers.abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene hosts strong correlation effects within topological flat bands separated from remote dispersive bands. This separation motivates projection onto the central bands, which greatly reduces the computational complexity of many-body calculations, including momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations. However, the interaction-induced Mott gap obtained in the projected model can be comparable to the noninteracting flat--remote band separation, raising the question of whether the projection remains valid. Here, we extend momentum-space QMC to explicitly include remote BM bands within a broad energy window at charge neutrality. We find that the projected description remains reliable over a broad parameter regime, up to $u_0/u_1\lesssim0.9$: the projected and remote-band calculations yield similar low-energy electron and trion spectra, and the Kramers intervalley-coherent ground state remains stable. In particular, the Dirac trion remains robust in the finite-temperature normal state when remote bands are included. Near the band-touching limit $u_0=u_1$, remote-band electrons acquire substantial low-energy spectral weight, accompanied by suppression of the trion weight and loss of the Kramers intervalley-coherent state. Our findings establish the broad validity of flat-band projection while reconciling the projected and THF viewpoints by identifying the near-band-touching regime in which explicit remote-band degrees of freedom become essential.
authors: Shibo Shan, Cheng Huang, Zi Yang Meng

papers.title: Algorithmic Quantum Sensing
papers.abstract: We introduce a unified framework for sensing time-dependent fields through the lens of classical and quantum algorithms. First, we develop three pulse sequence protocols, namely randomized, matched, and pooled spectroscopy, which outperform established approaches such as dynamical decoupling across a wide range of tasks. These protocols attain the optimal sensitivity for linear and nonlinear AC sensing on conventional spin or qubit platforms, improving existing devices by changing only their pulse sequences. We then introduce quantum computational spectroscopy (QCS), which couples quantum sensors to a quantum processor. QCS combines two new primitives: a quantum computational frequency comb that coherently converts any classical signal into a quantum oracle, and a family of quantum algorithms that use the oracle to extract signal information in superposition. Variations can be implemented on current platforms with only one memory ancilla. We show that the ultimate limit imposed by quantum mechanics lies polynomially beyond the Heisenberg limit, and that QCS achieves it. Attaining this new limit requires quantum computation, establishing a fundamental separation between conventional and quantum computational sensing. Moreover, QCS retains beyond-Heisenberg scaling for broadband signals under constant-strength sensor depolarization, while we prove that the same noise limits any protocol lacking quantum computation to standard-quantum-limit scaling. Our result provides the first asymptotic, beyond-quadratic quantum advantage in AC metrology when noise is aligned with the signal, proving that Lindblad span conditions do not apply to broadband quantum sensing. Our work builds an algorithmic theory for designing sensing protocols and establishes quantum sensing as a new frontier for quantum algorithms, with quantum advantages that surpass the Heisenberg limit and that persist under noise.
authors: Ishaan Kannan, Aditi Venkatesh, Jordan Cotler

papers.title: Structure and Binding of the \texorpdfstring{$pn\Omega^-$}{pnOmega} System with a Near-Unitary \texorpdfstring{$N\Omega$}{NOmega} Interaction from Physical-Point Lattice QCD
papers.abstract: The binding and spatial structure of the \(pn\Omega^-\) system are investigated in the \(I(J^P)=0(5/2^+)\) channel using the physical-point HAL QCD \(N\Omega({}^{5}S_2)\) interaction. The pairwise Hamiltonian includes the spin-triplet \(pn\) interaction and the finite-size Coulomb attraction in the \(p\Omega^-\) pair. The three-body Schr\"odinger equation is solved with the Gaussian Expansion Method (GEM), including all three Jacobi rearrangement configurations. For the central HAL QCD potential at \(t/a=14\), the calculated three-body binding energy is \(18.63\) MeV, corresponding to a separation energy of \(16.39\) MeV relative to the \(d+\Omega^-\) threshold. The spatial structure is examined through interparticle root-mean-square distances, pair and spectator radial distributions, and the correlation between the two Jacobi coordinates. Relative to a frozen-deuteron folded reference, the full three-body solution exhibits a substantially more compact spectator distribution and a contracted \(pn\) pair. The dependence on the Euclidean-time choice of the HAL QCD potential is also assessed. The results characterize the three-body rearrangement induced by the attractive \(N\Omega\) interaction within the adopted pairwise model.
authors: Faisal Etminan

papers.title: From Integrability to Chaos in Tensionless AdS3 String Theory
papers.abstract: We study quantum-gravitational corrections to the planar integrable structure of the symmetric product orbifold $\text{Sym}^N(\mathbb{T}^4)$ that is dual to tensionless string theory on AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times \mathbb{T}^4$. We consider the deformation that switches on R-R flux in the bulk, and analyze the associated level spacing statistics. The leading non-planar corrections lift the planar degeneracies and produce signs of random-matrix behavior. Our results provide a controlled example of string interactions driving the onset of quantum chaos.
authors: Matthias R. Gaberdiel, Beat Nairz, Cheng Peng

papers.title: QFT-Based Hybrid PointNet-Quantum Neural Networks for LiDAR Point-Cloud Classification
papers.abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical learning architectures provide a promising framework for integrating quantum feature transformations into complex data-processing tasks. Among these transformations, the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) offers a structured approach to feature processing, motivating an investigation of how its circuit configuration influences predictive performance, quantum resource requirements, and noise robustness. We present a hybrid PointNet-quantum neural network architecture for LiDAR point-cloud classification, combining classical feature extraction, amplitude encoding, and a variational quantum circuit. Five Fourier-processing configurations are systematically evaluated: No-QFT, Full-QFT-After, QFT-no-swap, IQFT-After, and Trainable-QFT. Experiments on KITTI, nuScenes, and PandaSet across three random seeds assess classification performance, class-level behavior, circuit complexity, and sensitivity to the IBM FakeManilaV2 noise model. Under ideal simulation, IQFT-After achieves the highest weighted F1-score on KITTI (0.857 $\pm$ 0.033), compared with 0.838 $\pm$ 0.023 for No-QFT. Removing the final SWAP gates in the QFT circuit reduces circuit complexity while preserving the Pauli-Z measurement features up to a fixed permutation that can be absorbed by the classification head. Under quantum noise, the circuit ranking changes, with IQFT-After exhibiting greater performance degradation and No-QFT and Trainable-QFT showing stronger robustness. Per-class analysis further identifies dataset-dependent differences in minority-class performance. These results demonstrate that Fourier-processing configuration influences both classification behavior and noise sensitivity, highlighting the role of circuit structure and hardware-aware evaluation in hybrid quantum learning for three-dimensional point-cloud data.
authors: Anurag Kulkarni, Nouhaila Innan, Muhammad Shafique

papers.title: Syndrome-based Calibration Using Gate-Error Amplification
papers.abstract: We present Gate-Error Amplification for Recalibration with Syndromes (GEARS), a runtime calibration framework that uses gate-error amplification to efficiently tune control parameters during quantum error correction. Maintaining reliable control of large qubit arrays throughout hours-long computations requires repeated calibration to compensate for hardware drift. In conventional calibration, targeted qubits are temporarily removed from the code, introducing non-negligible space-time overhead. An elegant alternative uses syndrome information already collected during error correction as feedback for in situ recalibration, but acquiring signal requires sufficient (1) measurement budget or (2) probe strength, i.e., the size of deliberate control perturbations. More measurements improve statistical precision but result in slower control updates, while stronger perturbations produce larger calibration signals at the cost of additional errors. GEARS augments syndrome-based calibration with an established gate characterization technique called gate-error amplification. Our approach repeats selected CZ gates and probes their controls in spatially separated groups, strengthening local calibration signals while limiting the logical cost of probing. Surface code simulations show that GEARS with depth-three amplification reduces measurement requirements by approximately a factor of eight at matched gradient SNR and fixed probe strength. In closed-loop calibration, GEARS with depth-three amplification reduces excess expected logical failures by approximately 31-40% relative to calibration without amplification across the evaluated execution windows. Under time-dependent drift, GEARS increases the estimated critical drift frequency by approximately 1.9x. These results indicate that deliberately amplifying gate errors during operation can improve the long-time performance of quantum computations.
authors: Andrew T. Kamen, Arielle Sanford, Frederic T. Chong, Andy J. Goldschmidt, Siddharth Dangwal

papers.title: A full-color four-point form factor
papers.abstract: We determine the symbol and complete functions of the full-color two-loop four-point maximally helicity violating stress-tensor form factor in $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, including $N^1$ double traces and $N^0$ single traces. Numerical unitarity and a master-integral bootstrap fix the result. A direct form-factor bootstrap reproduces the symbol. Permuting external legs in the planar 88-letter alphabet yields all 79 letters, while the $N^0$ terms contain four new nonclassical contributions. We also obtain the complete $N^0$ two-loop triple-collinear hard splitting functions.
authors: Song He, Xuhang Jiang

papers.title: Periods, isomonodromy, and modularity of ALG/ALG$^*$ gravitational instantons
papers.abstract: We prove that every smooth ALG or ALG$^*$ gravitational instanton of type $A_0,A_1,A_2,D_0,D_1,D_2,D_3$ is, up to homothety and hyperk\"ahler rotation, isometric to a rank-two wild Hitchin moduli space on $\PP^1$ with its $L^2$ metric. We compute the compact hyperk\"ahler periods and asymptotic parameters of these moduli spaces and give explicit inverse formulas for every admissible choice of these data. For the three ALG types, global isomonodromic transport realizes the two real parameters left undetermined by the compact periods. We use a Hamiltonian variation formula and uniform comparison with the semiflat metric to apply the Torelli and uniqueness theorems.
authors: Shiyu Cao

papers.title: Two Faces of Spacetime Density Matrices: Entanglement and Complexity
papers.abstract: We establish a direct connection between entanglement and complexity through spacetime density matrices. For stationary pure states and complementary regions at different times, spacetime replica moments encode the return amplitude of a replica-defect quench. This representation defines an associated state spread complexity, which we call Krylov-R\'enyi complexity. It can equivalently be obtained by using a replica-defect excitation of the replicated background state as the seed and evolving it under the original replicated Hamiltonian. We further construct Krylov-von Neumann complexity as a probe limit from first-order replica data. Timelike entanglement and complexity provide complementary information at a fixed time, while the full time dependence of the timelike entropy determines the Krylov dynamics and hence the complexity. The replica construction fixes the seed and its evolution through the background state, subsystem geometry, and regulator, without an independently chosen probe operator. Like entanglement entropy, the resulting complexity is defined nonperturbatively and probes universal properties and dynamical information about the underlying theory.
authors: Wu-zhong Guo

papers.title: Invariants of subfactors associated to Petrescu's Hadamard matrices of order 7
papers.abstract: Petrescu's sixth-root $7 \times 7$ Hadamard matrix defines an irreducible, hyperfinite subfactor $N \subset M$ with Jones index 7. It is built from the spin model commuting square obtained from the Hadamard matrix by iterating Jones' basic construction. We prove that the standard invariant of this subfactor is minimal, i.e. the higher relative commutants consists of Temperley-Lieb algebras. Thus, the principal graphs of the subfactor are the Coxeter-Dynkin graph A$_\infty$. This solves a long-standing open problem. The main new idea is a congruence for the profile of the Hadamard matrix that restricts the order of rotation on the lowest-weight spaces in Jones planar algebra description of the standard invariant. Together with a uniform trace bound, this gives bounded annular multiplicities on a subsequence, which forces the principal graph to have norm at most two. We also show that the same result holds for most Hadamard matrices in Petrescu's one-parameter family. Specifically, the associated subfactors have Temperley-Lieb standard invariant at every transcendental phase and at every algebraic phase with residue $\pm1$ at a prime above three. In each fixed degree the exceptional set is finite and consists of algebraic numbers. Our methods apply to several other families of Hadamard matrices of order $q >4$ as well, and we show that the associated subfactors have A$_\infty$ principal graphs. These include real Hadamard matrices of order $q\equiv4\pmod8$, Hadamard matrices over $\Q(i)$ of order $q\equiv2\pmod4$ and cube-root matrices of order $q$ with $3\mid q$ and $9\nmid q$. For order six Hadamard matrices, we obtain the same result at every transcendental phase in Di\c{t}\u{a}'s family through Haagerup's matrix and at every algebraically independent pair of phases in Karlsson's two-parameter family.
authors: Dietmar Bisch, Remus Nicoara

papers.title: Asymptotics of Hitchin metrics and modularity of exceptional ALG gravitational instantons
papers.abstract: We prove asymptotic estimates for the Hitchin metrics on four-dimensional moduli spaces of parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(n,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere with flag types corresponding to the Dynkin types $E_6$, $E_7$ and $E_8$. For fixed weights in the alcove interiors and fixed scalar graded residues, the Hitchin metric converges in $C^\infty$ to the semiflat metric along the end. The decay is polynomial in general and exponential when all graded residues vanish. For every admissible parameter with weights in the closed alcoves, the moduli space with its Hitchin metric is a complete nonflat ALG gravitational instanton of order two. Extending the period calculation of Dimakis--Fredrickson--Yae to the boundary and allowing compactly supported changes of marking, we obtain every point of the normalized period domain. It follows from the ALG Torelli theorem that every ALG gravitational instanton with cone parameter $1/3$, $1/4$ or $1/6$ is isometric, up to homothety and hyperk\"ahler rotation, to one of these moduli spaces with its Hitchin metric.
authors: Shiyu Cao

papers.title: Correctable Enrollment and One-Transaction Seed Proofs for Ethereum's Post-Quantum Transition
papers.abstract: A quantum computer running Shor's algorithm can extract the private key of every Ethereum account whose public key is published, and accounts exposed by their own transactions hold 54.6% of execution-layer ETH. As the first such machine may stay secret, a migration cannot wait for visible thefts, and once keys are extractable, legacy signatures no longer tell owners from attackers. We design a migration in which owners enroll post-quantum keys cheaply with their existing signatures before ECDSA is retired at a scheduled time, while a zero-knowledge proof of the wallet's BIP-39 seed can correct any such enrollment until a common deadline afterward; an account nobody enrolled stays frozen and recoverable by seed proof without a deadline. Each proof binds the new key, a nonce and a fee cap, so neither a paying sponsor nor a reordering block builder can redirect or replay it. Validators switch to hash-based keys first, at a finalized checkpoint and under a stated bound on the attacker's voting power. We prove the account guarantees under explicit assumptions, model-check the rules, and implement the design in go-ethereum and a Lean consensus client. A three-layer recursive hash-based STARK yields a seed proof of about 190 KB that fits one transaction, verifies in 38 ms and takes a median of 111 s to generate on a laptop; four proofs aggregate into one. In a ten-node simulation with mainnet-derived accounts and fee demand, block space rather than proving sets the duration: the 4.45 million accounts with at least 0.1 ETH would migrate in 29.4 days if all enroll before ECDSA is retired and in 235 days if all recover after it in batches of four. In a mass enrollment, an enrollment waits a median of 19.1 minutes in the public mempool, longer than published estimates for a fast quantum computer to extract its key, so owners with a seed and an unexposed key should migrate by seed proof.
authors: Xin Jin, Maximillian Liao, Handong Chen, Yi Nancy Li, Junyu Liu

papers.title: Propagation of chaos with singular potentials: A weighted duality approach
papers.abstract: We establish the propagation of chaos and derive the Vlasov equation from a many-body $N$-particle system in the mean-field regime with singular interaction forces bounded by $|x|^{-\alpha-1}$ for $0\le \alpha <(d-1)/2$ in dimensions $d\ge 2$, which in particular include the full range of sub-Coulomb interactions in three dimensions as well as the Coulomb interaction in two dimensions. Our proof is based on an energy-based framework for deriving weighted uniform bounds on cumulants that builds upon the recent duality method developed by Bresch--Duerinckx--Jabin in combination with a new Morawetz-type estimate, allowing us to remove the restriction to locally square-integrable interaction force kernels and handle more singular regimes.
authors: Phan Th\`anh Nam, Toan T. Nguyen

papers.title: Insurance portfolio simulation with a quantum circuit
papers.abstract: A central challenge in actuarial science is characterising the distribution of losses generated by an insurance portfolio. Copulas provide a natural framework for modelling joint distributions, but flexible high-dimensional copula fitting and sampling remains challenging in practice. We propose a Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) approach adapted to insurance portfolios, combining (i) a tail-focused discretisation of heavy-tailed marginals, (ii) a Monte Carlo-style objective function that enables the numerical precision of the algorithm to scale when trained on a relatively small number of samples, and (iii) a two-stage hierarchical training scheme enabling efficient training on a simulator and fine-tuning on quantum hardware. On a mixed portfolio of equity returns and insurance losses, the trained circuit recovers the qualitative dependence structure, with near-independence between equity and losses and positive dependence among loss lines. Exponential quantile encoding substantially improves the fit to the tail of the aggregate loss distribution relative to a uniform encoding, and the hierarchical scheme substantially outperforms single-stage training of a circuit of the same size from random initialisation.
authors: William Cashman, Marco Caselli, Saad Hamid, Daniel Mills, Pavel Stishenko

papers.title: Supersymmetric Hilbert complexes and Witten deformation on stratified pseudomanifolds
papers.abstract: We present a framework to study topics related to index theory and Dirac operators with N=1,2 supersymmetry (SUSY), extending it to stratified pseudomanifolds with wedge metrics (iterated conic metrics). We use this to construct Witten deformed subcomplexes of SUSY Hilbert complexes that categorify Morse polynomials and equivariant index formulae for a large class of operators. This allows us to prove equivariant index theorems for spin-c Dirac operators with Hamiltonian actions, and Holomorphic Morse inequalities in the K\"ahler case, in particular proving a new type of equivariant Riemann-Roch (ERR) theorem on singular spaces. We also improve on stratified Morse-Bott inequalities in the de Rham case, and review other applications including for the Kervaire semi-characteristic and the equivariant signature. We compute local cohomology groups for the Dolbeault complexes at both smooth and singular non-isolated fixed point sets which categorify the ERR numbers. In an Appendix joint with Alex R. Taylor, we give a broad overview of the relevance of SUSY to index theory on manifolds with boundaries and singularities, mainly focusing on the new insights and results related to N=2 SUSY that the authors have uncovered recently.
authors: Gayana Jayasinghe, Manousos Maridakis, Hadrian Quan, Alex R. Taylor, Xinran Yu

papers.title: Parallel transversal entangling gates for fault-tolerant trapped-ion quantum computing
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires high-fidelity entangling gates that can be implemented efficiently across multiple qubit pairs. We present a scheme for simultaneous pairwise entangling operations, i.e., a transversal controlled-$Z$ gate, across neighboring wells in a double-well trapped-ion architecture. A tailored dynamical decoupling scheme suppresses unwanted couplings with a pulse count that scales quadratically with the number of ions. We show that incorporating a genuine geometric cancellation reduces the pulse count and, for selected register sizes, allows the parallel operation to be completed faster than an equivalent sequence of two-qubit gates while requiring a significantly smaller two-photon Rabi frequency. We assess the experimental feasibility of the protocol by analyzing the impact of decoherence and crosstalk arising from laser wave-vector misalignment. To gain insight into the robustness of fault-tolerant protocols against realistic imperfections of the proposed transversal gate scheme, we investigate how crosstalk-induced gate errors affect the fault-tolerant preparation of a logical Bell state between two $[[4,1,2]]$ quantum-error-detection code blocks. These results highlight the potential of transversal entangling gates as a building block for trapped-ion-based scalable fault-tolerant quantum error correction.
authors: Katrin Bolsmann, Alan Kahan, Alejandro Berm\'udez, Markus M\"uller

papers.title: Second-order formulation of chiral fermions with a local boundary condition
papers.abstract: Chiral fermions in $d$ dimensions arise naturally as boundary modes of a massive fermion in $d+1$ dimensions subject to a local boundary condition. When anomalies are absent, this construction can be used to define an intrinsically $d$-dimensional theory of chiral fermions. However, defining the path integral using the first-order Dirac operator with this boundary condition is technically inconvenient, even in the continuum. We present a formulation in terms of second-order differential operators that is completely equivalent to the original formulation in the continuum. Its natural lattice discretization generates Wilson's term and avoids fermion doubling. Our lattice formulation closely resembles the boundary-fermion construction of Shamir, and provides some insight into the case of a general Wilson parameter.
authors: Kazuya Yonekura

papers.title: Beyond Error Mitigation: Using Boosting for Noisy Quantum Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Quantum error mitigation (QEM) can recover information about ideal quantum computations from noisy circuit executions, but may require a large sampling overhead. Fundamental lower bounds show that recovering noiseless observables without problem-specific information can require superpolynomially many samples, with exponential overhead for broad classes of noisy circuits. However, problem-specific information can reduce the number of samples needed to obtain the required answer. We investigate this possibility in supervised quantum machine learning, where labeled examples provide information about the function to be learned. Binary classification provides such a setting, since correct prediction depends on the sign and margin of the classifier output rather than on accurate reconstruction of every noiseless expectation value. We develop a theoretical and empirical framework for comparing boosting of noisy parameterized quantum circuits with probabilistic error cancellation (PEC), requiring both methods to reach the same learning target. For the specified circuit architectures under Pauli noise, we establish a common hypothesis-class complexity bound: matching empirical margin loss gives the same upper bound on expected classification risk. We derive resource criteria and evaluate AdaBoostR and Real AdaBoost in finite-shot teacher-student simulations across circuit depth and physical noise strength. Under the same classification-accuracy target, boosting requires fewer circuit executions as depth and noise increase. Boosting also achieves higher test accuracy than the corresponding reference. For the supervised-learning problems studied, these results demonstrate a task-dependent resource advantage: exploiting information retained in noisy outputs can avoid the cost of ideal-output reconstruction without sacrificing observed classification performance.
authors: Anastasiia Lukianenko, Yash J. Patel, Nurbolat Kenbayev, Vedran Dunjko

papers.title: Global-in-Time Nonrelativistic Limit and KAM Tori for the Complex Klein-Gordon Equation on the Circle
papers.abstract: This paper establishes a global-in-time nonrelativistic limit for families of small-amplitude quasi-periodic solutions of the cubic complex Klein-Gordon equation on the circle. Firstly, we construct by a KAM block scheme, small-amplitude two-frequency invariant tori and show that their linear stability depends on whether the two excited Fourier indices coincide or are distinct: coincident indices yield linearly stable tori, whereas distinct indices yield partially hyperbolic tori. Moreover, controlling the dependence of the KAM scheme on the speed of light, we construct quasi-periodic solutions whose frequencies, after a gauge transformation, coincide exactly with those of quasi-periodic solutions of the limiting coupled NLS system, obtaining an approximation uniform for all times in the nonrelativistic regime. By this result, we further show that there exists a positive-measure set of frequencies such that, for each frequency, we can fix a quasi-periodic solution of the coupled NLS system and a suitable subsequence of Klein-Gordon solutions converging globally in time to the fixed NLS solution.
authors: Andrea Belloni

papers.title: Critical droplets and metastability in long-range chains
papers.abstract: Metastable decay in first-order phase transitions proceeds through the nucleation of critical droplets. In the one-dimensional nearest-neighbor Ising chain, the cost of the two walls bounding a droplet is independent of its size. For interactions decaying as $1/r^{1+\sigma}$, this surface cost instead depends on the droplet size and competes with the bulk free-energy gain. The critical radius scales as $R_c\propto h^{-1/\sigma}$ at small $h$, where $h>0$ is the bias field. The value $\sigma=1$ separates two regimes: for $\sigma<1$, the activation barrier diverges as $h\to0^+$; at $\sigma=1$, it grows logarithmically; and for $\sigma>1$, it remains finite, as in the nearest-neighbor chain. A nonlocal $\phi^4$ field theory yields critical droplets with algebraic tails and confirms the predicted radius and barrier scalings, while stochastic long-range dynamics independently reproduces the critical-radius scaling.
authors: Laura Batini, Valerio Pagni, Nicol\`o Defenu

papers.title: Block decimation and perfect actions for $p$-adic valued path integrals
papers.abstract: In earlier work we introduced a finite-partition propagator for $\mathbb{C}_p$-valued wave functions, in which the intermediate positions are integrated against atomic measures. The iterated integral evaluates the action on the equally spaced chain between the endpoints, so each partition level is obtained by iterating an exact, tree-level block decimation of two-point lattice actions, with no integration over fluctuations. This kinematic decimation is the Fr\'echet derivative, at the free actions, of the variational decimation underlying classical perfect actions. Since the time step $p^n$ is small in the real norm exactly when it is large $p$-adically, refinement and coarsening (the ultraviolet and infrared directions over $\mathbb{R}$) exchange roles, and each yields one limit. Under refinement, potentials supported on $\mathbb{Z}_p$, given there by a convergent power series, and entering the slice action without the time-step weight produce an interaction that stabilizes off the diagonal after finitely many steps and converges uniformly on $\mathbb{Z}_p^2$, with sharp error $p^{-M}$ after $M$ steps, to a scale-covariant (perfect) action, governed near the diagonal by a Volkenborn integral; with the weight no limit exists. For the harmonic oscillator no refinement limit exists at fixed frequency, but under coarsening the variational flow is solved in closed form: the lattice angle is multiplied by $p$ at each step, the coupling obeys a Chebyshev recursion, no caustic occurs, and the rescaled action converges to a free action with renormalized mass $m_0\sin_p(\theta_0)/\theta_0$. The rescaled linearized map is diagonalizable on polynomial actions with eigenvalues $p^{2-b}$, so directions relevant over $\mathbb{R}$ are irrelevant over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and conversely.
authors: Su Hu, Min-Soo Kim

papers.title: Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Differential Privacy
papers.abstract: Differential privacy has been successfully extended to quantum computing and information processing, where sensitive data are encoded in quantum states and protected by quantum noise mechanisms that keep the outcomes of any measurement on neighboring states nearly indistinguishable. In the quantum setting, however, the state submitted to a quantum computer may be entangled with a hidden reference system secretly held by an adversary. Such entanglement cannot be detected from the submitted state alone, and it poses a challenge with no counterpart in the classical setting. Existing frameworks of quantum differential privacy consider only measurements on the released state, leaving this scenario largely unexplored. In this paper, we identify the entanglement attack: an adversary submits one half of an entangled state to a quantum computer that runs a privacy mechanism, keeps the other half, and finally measures both halves jointly. We show that this attack may completely break a mechanism that satisfies quantum differential privacy with a finite parameter, driving its privacy parameter to infinity. To counter it, we propose entanglement-assisted quantum differential privacy (EA-QDP), a privacy framework that is native to quantum entanglement and remains valid against such attacks. We characterize exactly when a mechanism has a finite EA-QDP parameter, and show that the optimal parameter $\varepsilon^*_{\mathrm{EA}}$ of any quantum mechanism can be computed by a semidefinite programming problem (SDP). Building on this, we quantify the extra privacy leakage caused by entanglement and show that it can be bounded by choosing appropriate mechanisms, with the depolarizing channel being our recommended choice. Finally, we demonstrate both the attack and its countermeasure on simulated and physical quantum hardware, and the experimental results agree with our theoretical predictions.
authors: Chenjian Li, Ji Guan, Mingsheng Ying

papers.title: Structure-Guided Synthesis of Low-Error Syndrome Extraction Circuits
papers.abstract: Gate orders can change fault propagation and logical error rates even when syndrome-extraction circuits implement the same ideal stabilizer measurements. Optimizing these orderings independently for every check, however, becomes computationally demanding as code size increases. We present a synthesis method for structured Calderbank-Shor-Steane codes that groups checks by recurring connectivity and shares one relative gate order per group, reducing independent ordering choices. A CP-SAT solver jointly determines the shared orders and the execution time of each physical gate, enforcing resource and measurement constraints across the circuit. Noisy circuit simulations with decoding then guide the selection of the final circuit. We compare with state-of-the-art approaches, including Auto-Stabilizer-Check (ASC), PropHunt, and AlphaSyndrome. Across 15 quantum low-density parity-check codes from ten code families, our method achieves the lowest logical error rate estimates. Relative to ASC, the strongest baseline in our evaluation, the median reduction is 11.4% and the largest is 38.6%. Our circuits improve circuit-level distance over ASC on ten instances and preserve the code distance in seven. Across five timed codes, our method reduces the mean time to the first feasible circuit by factors of 21.4-136.6 relative to ASC, at equal or lower depth.
authors: Shanchuan Li, Xin Hong, Pengcheng Zhu, Xiangzhen Zhou, Fanxu Meng, Shenggang Ying

papers.title: Moir\'e-Enabled Recursive Phase Unwrapping for Differential Atom Interferometry
papers.abstract: Weak equivalence principle tests comparing different elements may be more sensitive to violations than those comparing isotopes. However, differences in effective wave vector complicate common-mode rejection of vibration noise. We propose a Moir\'e-enabled recursive phase unwrapping (MRPU) method for differential measurements with dual-species atom interferometers. The method exploits the moir\'e structure of the joint phase likelihood and temporal acceleration correlations to unwrap both phases and determine the relative acceleration. We implemented an $^{85}$Rb $\mathrm{D_1/D_2}$ line dual-scale-factor interferometer with an identical normalized transfer function and a large effective wave-vector difference to emulate different atomic species. Under $40\,\mathrm{rad}$ equivalent vibrational noise, this method achieved phase unwrapping over 5000 consecutive measurements, with a relative-acceleration Allan deviation of $1.47\times10^{-8}g$ at 997 shots. Numerical simulations under random vibrations and slow drifts show a $9.76 - 26.03\,\mathrm{dB}$ increase in the tolerable narrowband vibration amplitude. This method is promising for weak equivalence principle tests based on different atomic species, dark matter and dark energy detection, and high-dynamic-range atomic gravimetry.
authors: Junjie Jiang, Sitong Yan, Jiaming Wei, Chuan He, Xi Chen, Lin Zhou, Jin Wang, Ming-Sheng Zhan

papers.title: Precise experimental investigation of the reflection properties caused by s-polarized evanescent waves and the Casimir puzzle
papers.abstract: We report a high-precision experiment on measuring the low-frequency magnetic field reflected from a metallic plate. This experiment is designed to give insight into why theoretical predictions of the fundamental Lifshitz theory using the standard response function to the electromagnetic waves are in contradiction with the data of numerous precision measurements of the Casimir force (the Casimir puzzle). To attain these ends, we measured the magnitude and phase of the lateral component of the magnetic field produced by an oscillating magnetic dipole and reflected from a metallic plate. These quantities are completely determined by the evanescent waves with the transverse electric (s) polarization. The obtained measurement data are compared with theoretical predictions using the standard Drude response function of the metal to the low-frequency electromagnetic waves. It is shown that there are both quantitative and qualitative disagreements with these predictions, so that in the region of low-frequency s-polarized evanescent waves the Drude response function is excluded by the data. Keeping in mind that just the s-polarized evanescent waves are responsible for the Casimir puzzle, our results highlight the causes for its emergence. It is emphasized that, in addition to the Casimir effect, searching for the adequate nonlocal response functions of metals to the evanescent waves is of utmost significance for many areas of physics as near-field optical microscopy, nanophotonics, surface plasmon polaritons, radiative heat transfer, and others.
authors: M. Dhital, G. L. Klimchitskaya, V. M. Mostepanenko, U. Mohideen

papers.title: Nonmagnetic Impurity Effects on Majorana Braiding Quantum Gates in Vortex Cores
papers.abstract: Using time-dependent many-body simulations, we investigate nonmagnetic impurity effects on vortex-core Majorana braiding. In the two-MZM $\sqrt{Z}$ gate, sufficiently strong attractive impurities suppress the topological gap $\Delta_t$, reduce adiabaticity, and degrade the quantization of the geometric-phase difference; the repulsive impurities considered here cause no comparable damage despite stronger zero-energy nonequilibrium local density of states (LDOS) distortions. Slowing the braid or using a $2a_0$ detour restores near-quantization in the cases examined. In the four-MZM configuration, attractive impurities leave the low-energy spectrum nearly unchanged, whereas repulsive impurities mainly suppress the first excited state. Slower braiding substantially improves the $X$ gate success probability. A specific attractive-impurity pair yields near-unit success ($\approx 0.9985$), unlike two weak repulsive impurities. These findings clarify how nonmagnetic impurities affect the low-energy spectrum and adiabatic dynamics of vortex-core Majorana braiding and provide theoretical guidance for designing robust braiding protocols in realistic topological superconducting platforms.
authors: Jiangwei Long, Zihui Liu, Yizhi Li, Lijun Meng

papers.title: Majorana dark matter from a thick-to-thin brane junction: Modal stability, real-mediator coannihilation, and a dark-radiation imprint
papers.abstract: We show that the localized spectrum of a $D=7$ thick-to-thin brane junction can host a thermal Majorana dark-matter candidate. The anisotropy of the wall widths isolates a light junction fermion, which a four-dimensional Majorana mass splits into two nearby states. The factorized transverse profiles impose a modal selection rule on all cubic couplings, and together with the relaxation of the softly deformed background this makes the lighter state stable without an imposed dark parity. Because the localized mediator is a real scalar, identical Majorana particles annihilate in the $s$ wave, and the relic coupling becomes nearly independent of the Majorana mass. The junction sector is a Standard-Model singlet whose light chiral mode is a source of dark radiation. Current CMB data restrict its decoupling temperature and imply $0.05\lesssim\dNeff\lesssim0.076$ for dark-matter masses between $10\GeV$ and $1.5\TeV$, a range accessible to next-generation CMB surveys.
authors: F. A. Brito

papers.title: Evolving Decoding Algorithms for Quantum Error Correction
papers.abstract: Quantum computation entails robustness engineering: a noisy quantum state is measured continuously, and a classical algorithm (the decoder) must infer corrections that reliably remove the noise, fast enough to keep up. We write several published belief-propagation (BP) decoders for quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes in a Domain-Specific Language (DSL), and search over it with grammatical evolution. Written in the language, the published decoders show their parameters in plain view, allowing us to re-parameterise BP+OSD (ordered statistics decoding) and BP+LSD (localized statistics decoding) decoders with damping, before any search, making each 17.1--41.0$\times$ faster at a higher error rate, and BP+OSD-0 about 103 faster than the ldpc package's version tuned on the [[72,12,6]] bivariate-bicycle code. Evolution over the language finds decoders that improve the time-error front. One makes 23% fewer logical errors than BP+OSD-0 with damping at 0.64$\times$ its time, and decoders evolved from random code are more accurate than ldpc's tuned BP+OSD-0 at 1/31 of its time or less. Frozen at one operating point, the two fastest evolved decoders generalize well across noise levels, code sizes and round counts, staying at the time-error front. Ultimately, we demonstrate that capturing expert knowledge within a DSL creates a powerful intermediate layer---one that effectively bridges human intuition and machine-driven optimization to unlock highly efficient quantum error correction.
authors: Eduardo Due\~nez, Edgar Said Hernandez Sanchez, Edgar A. Du\'e\~nez-Guzm\'an, Suzanne Sadedin

papers.title: Higher-order magnetic hopfions in uniaxial chiral magnets
papers.abstract: Chiral magnets host hopfions, but their experimentally observed configurations are largely limited to hopfion rings, heliknotons, and their clusters. Here, we show that uniaxial anisotropy stabilizes a diverse family of knotted and linked hopfions with zero and arbitrary positive Hopf indices. We identify their stability regions in the anisotropy -- field parameter space and introduce a systematic construction based on mapping skyrmion braids into three-dimensional magnetic textures. We find that the minimum energy of stable hopfions increases approximately linearly with the Hopf index.
authors: Vladyslav M. Kuchkin, Nikolai S. Kiselev

papers.title: Scaling limits for products of induced symplectic Ginibre matrices
papers.abstract: We study the local eigenvalue correlations of products of independent induced symplectic Ginibre matrices in the large-dimensional limit. We establish the scaling limits of the correlation functions in the bulk, at the spectral edges, and outside the limiting spectral support, both near and away from the real axis. At regular spectral points, we show that the limiting correlations coincide with those of a single symplectic Ginibre ensemble, exhibiting Pfaffian structures near the real axis and determinantal structures away from it. At the origin, where the limiting spectral density develops a singularity, we derive an integral representation of the parameter-dependent limiting Pfaffian prekernel. Our proofs are based on a unified approach involving a differential equation for the skew prekernels and their asymptotics.
authors: Can Atacan, Noah Ayg\"un, Yong-Woo Lee

papers.title: High-fidelity control of long-lived data qubits via a noisy mediator
papers.abstract: Long-lived qubits are attractive for storing quantum information, but they are often difficult to control or couple directly. A common strategy is to use mediator qubits to generate effective interactions for gate implementation. However, the mediator typically has a shorter coherence time than the data qubits, so mediator relaxation and dephasing are expected to limit the achievable gate fidelity. Here, we show that this limitation can be overcome. We present a reset-assisted control method that suppresses mediator-induced errors and enables high-fidelity single- and two-qubit gates on a quantum register of long-lived data qubits. Although mediator quantum jumps render the data-qubit evolution stochastic, repeated mediator reinitialization drives the resulting evolution paths toward the desired target operation. An analytical quantum-trajectory analysis reveals the physical mechanism of error suppression and provides compact fidelity formulas for adapting the method to different platforms. Our results relax the requirement for long mediator coherence, broadening the range of mediators that can support high-fidelity control.
authors: Nguyen H. Le, Tikai Chang, Eran Ginossar, Michael Stern

papers.title: A Quantum Genetic Algorithm for Optimization of Benchmark Test Functions using Entangled Qutrits
papers.abstract: Typically, quantum genetic algorithms are based on qubits, a two-level quantum system. This work investigates the optimization of Rastrigin, Rosen-Brock and Table Holder Function in comparison with Classical Genetic Algorithm (CGA), using two quantum approaches: Quantum Genetic Algorithm (QGA), and Higher-Order Quantum Genetic Algorithm (HO-QGA) based on qutrits, a three-level system. HO-QGA uses higher-dimensional quantum representations, such as entangled qutrits, to test its capability of enhanced optimization. We show that the QGA convergence rate is higher than the CGA, and the solution quality is considerably improved. Based on this study, a three-state quantum object novelly provides more capabilities than qubits in terms of computational and information resources.
authors: Muhammad Farooq, Mehrosh Talat

papers.title: Equation of state of hot and dense QCD at the physical point via the complex Langevin equation
papers.abstract: This study presents the first results for the equation of state of 2+1+1-flavor QCD at the physical point, obtained using the complex Langevin equation. We calculate continuum-extrapolated thermodynamic quantities, such as the baryon density, pressure, the speed of sound and the adiabatic compressibility. The simulations are performed in the isospin-symmetric, strangeness- and charm-neutral setting above the crossover temperature and at unprecedentedly large baryon chemical potentials.
authors: Michael Mandl, D\'enes Sexty, Daniel Unterhuber

papers.title: Optimal long-time derivative estimates for underdamped Langevin dynamics
papers.abstract: We study the long-time behaviour of derivatives of the semigroup $P_t=e^{t\mathcal{A}}$ generated by the underdamped Langevin (kinetic Fokker-Planck) operator $\mathcal{A}$ on $L^2(\mu)$, where the Gibbs measure $\mu$ is not required to be finite. Under a weighted relative bound on the Hessian of the potential, we prove that for every integer $m\ge 0$ the squared $L^2(\mu)$ norms of $\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ and of $\nabla_{x,v}\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ are bounded by $C_m t^{-2m}\|h_0\|^2$ and $D_m t^{-(2m+1)}\|h_0\|^2$ respectively for large times, and the free dynamics shows that these exponents are optimal. The proof rests on a resolvent estimate near the imaginary axis, valid for every smooth potential, which follows from the adjoint relation between the generator and the velocity reversal and from the Gaussian Poincar\'e inequality in the velocity variable.
authors: Lukang Sun

papers.title: A New Quantum Algorithm Framework for Integer Order Entropy Estimation
papers.abstract: Entropy estimation for unknown distributions is a basic problem in statistical property estimation. In this paper, we propose a quantum algorithm framework for estimating R\'enyi entropy with fixed integer order $k\geq 2$. Given purified quantum query-access to a distribution on $n$ symbols, our algorithm estimates its order-$k$ R\'enyi entropy to within additive error $\epsilon$ using $$\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\frac{n^{u_k}}{\epsilon^{1-u_k}} + \frac{n^{(k-1)/(2k)}}\epsilon\right)$$ queries, where $u_k=\max_{2\leq j\leq k} \frac{(3k-j)2^{j-2}-k}{k(2^j-1)}$. The main ingredient is a recursive construction of collision states in which intermediate states are retained and reused. We bound both the preparation and reflection costs, and choose the number of retained states at each order so that all recursive steps fit within a common query budget. We combine this construction with a sequence of decreasing probability thresholds, estimating the contribution of the labels found along the way separately from the remaining power sum. A batch estimator gives the required bound in the high-precision regime, and an initial search removes the need for prior knowledge of the power sum.
authors: Zongxing Xiong

papers.title: Holographic Tessellations Tensor Networks $\{p,q\}$ from Entangled Quantum Tetrahedron in Loop Quantum Gravity
papers.abstract: The relationship between spin network states in loop quantum gravity and bulk--boundary duality is further explored using the tessellated holographic tensor network. We develop a holographic tensor network construction based on quantum entanglement between tetrahedra in loop quantum gravity (LQG). This construction relates four-valent intertwiner spaces and Bell states dressed with $SU(2)$ holonomies to effective tensors on hyperbolic $\{p,q\}$ tessellations. For the $\{5,4\}$ tessellation, six tetrahedra are assembled into a single effective cell with five network legs and one logical index. Provided that the microscopic transfer map has full row rank, a right inverse and a completion on the kernel space are employed to construct an isometric embedding, yielding an effective tensor proportional to a perfect tensor. The construction is generalized to the $p=2n-1$ family, with local dimensions supporting absolutely maximally entangled states. On finite networks satisfying a radial orientation condition, an appropriate normalization produces an isometric bulk--boundary map. For cuts satisfying the isometry condition on both sides, the boundary entropy decomposes into a link contribution $\sum_{\ell}\log(2j_{\ell}+1)$ and the bulk entropy, thereby providing a discrete realization of the quantum Ryu--Takayanagi structure. Applications to the black hole interior are formulated via postselection-based non-isometric encoding. Assuming additional Haar statistics, this framework is used to analyze the preservation of overlaps on average and the competition between entropy branches underlying the Page Curve. These results establish a constructive link between the geometric degrees of freedom of LQG and holographic codes, while clarifying the conditions required to connect them to geometric area in LQG, the location of the quantum extremal surface, and evaporation of black hole.
authors: Deden M. Akbar, Freddy P. Zen, Jusak S. Kosasih

papers.title: Flat bands and bound states in the continuum in non-Hermitian pseudospin lattices
papers.abstract: Flat bands support compact localized states (CLSs), whereas bound states in the continuum (BICs) remain spatially localized despite having energies embedded in the continuum of extended states. Here, we investigate the connection between these phenomena in a class of one-dimensional non-Hermitian lattices whose Bloch Hamiltonians take the pseudospin form H(k)=d(k)S. For integer pseudospin, the Hamiltonian intrinsically supports a zero-energy flat band and its associated compact localized states. When the effective pseudospin field has real transverse components and a purely imaginary longitudinal component, increasing non-Hermiticity compresses the dispersive bands toward the intrinsic zero-energy flat band, enabling their spectral overlap within a finite parameter range. The CLSs thus become embedded in the dispersive continuum and emerge as BICs. Adding a momentum-dependent Hermitian component along the gain-loss direction generally removes this spectral overlap without destroying the CLSs. We further extend this spectral mechanism to integer-pseudospin-n systems. These findings establish a connection between intrinsic flat-band localization and BIC formation through non-Hermitian spectral reconstruction.
authors: X. Y. Chen, C. H. Zhang
