papers.title: The influence of quantum scarring on the onset of Bohmian chaos
papers.abstract: In the present work we investigate how the stable and unstable periodic orbits of a perturbed two-dimensional oscillator influence the Bohmian trajectories of the corresponding quantum system. In particular, we find that in our systems all Bohmian trajectories become chaotic in the long run and examine the times needed for them to approach their ergodic pattern. We show that these times are systematically shorter for orbits close to unstable periodic orbits than for orbits close to stable periodic orbits of the same period. We demonstrate that this behaviour is connected to scarring effects associated with both unstable and stable periodic orbits. We also investigate how the Bohmian dynamics changes when a stable periodic orbit undergoes a bifurcation and becomes unstable.
authors: Athanasios C. Tzemos, George Contopoulos

papers.title: Worldsheet Effective Theory of Abelian-Higgs Cosmic Strings beyond Nambu--Goto
papers.abstract: Cosmic strings can support long-lived excitations confined to their cores, opening channels for energy exchange with the transverse Goldstone modes that describe the string's motion. We derive a covariant worldsheet theory of their coupled dynamics directly from the Abelian-Higgs model at critical coupling, with all interaction coefficients fixed by the microscopic theory. The resulting action, which we validate against numerical lattice field theory simulations, extends the Nambu--Goto description to include a massive scalar shape mode and a massive vector mode. Dualizing the vector reveals a geometric distinction: the shape scalar mode couples to intrinsic worldsheet curvature, while the pseudoscalar couples to normal bundle curvature. These interactions explain the distinct parametric instabilities observed in lattice simulations and predict how the relative polarization of colliding transverse waves controls the excitation of the two internal modes. Our results connect microscopic string structure to the nonlinear worldsheet dynamics, providing a predictive framework for cosmic strings beyond the Nambu--Goto approximation.
authors: Sergio Alameda-Calvo, Josu C. Aurrekoetxea, Jose J. Blanco-Pillado, Alberto Garc\'ia Mart\'in-Caro, J. M. Queiruga

papers.title: Finite-Key Analysis for Multiple-Antenna Quantum Key Distribution with Continuous Variables
papers.abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) techniques, known for their use in wireless communications, can also find applications in quantum communications systems. This is, for instance, relevant to satellite-based quantum communications when atmospheric turbulence and the time-varying nature of the channel can make their implementation difficult. Here, we study the application of MIMO techniques to continuous-variable (CV) quantum key distribution (QKD) in the realistic setting where a finite number of signals are exchanged. We show how data collected during the brief overpass time of low-earth-orbit satellites over ground stations can be processed to estimate MIMO channel parameters, extract a secret key, and quantify the key generation rate. For $2\times 2$ MIMO settings with Gaussian encoding and heterodyne detection, our finite-key analysis indicates that MIMO CV-QKD could outperform both multiplexed (with a nominal 3~dB improvement) and single-mode (with a nominal 6~dB nominal improvement) scenarios. Furthermore, we conjecture that the ultimate enhancement of a multiple-antenna CV-QKD system can be characterized by the product of the number of its inputs and outputs.
authors: Masoud Ghalaii, Ahmed Q. Lawey, Mohsen Razavi

papers.title: Galaxy Bias and Soft Limits from Inflation
papers.abstract: Primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG) leaves an imprint on large-scale structure through a scale-dependent galaxy bias, and properly incorporating the effects of higher order PNG into the bias expansion requires a consistent renormalization framework that extends beyond the squeezed limit of the bispectrum. We develop the multi-loop renormalization of bias operators in the presence of non-vanishing primordial n-point functions of arbitrary order, including stochastic contributions. We show that galaxy bias renormalization is determined by the multi-soft limits of primordial correlators and bias kernels. We provide explicit computations for one- and two-loop renormalization of deterministic operators up to fifth order in the bias expansion. Finally, we derive the renormalization group equations for the bias parameters at one and two loops.
authors: Charalampos Nikolis, Henrique Rubira

papers.title: Equilibrium relativistic spin magnetohydrodynamics from chiral kinetic theory
papers.abstract: We develop a microscopic and thermodynamically consistent framework for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics of massless chiral fermions, directly from first-order chiral kinetic theory. Starting from the covariant Wigner function, we recast the chiral kinetic equation as a pure streaming equation on a magnetically shifted mass shell, incorporating both the magnetic-moment energy and the Berry-curvature phase-space measure. This formulation yields a kinetic $H$-theorem and an entropy current with vanishing divergence in global equilibrium. We construct the equilibrium distribution for an arbitrary spin frame and derive the associated currents, energy--momentum tensor, spin tensor, entropy current, and frame-independent spin polarization, including the magnetic splitting between particles and antiparticles. Thermodynamic consistency further determines the second-order magnetovortical responses, revealing a relativistic Barnett magnetization, a temperature- and chemical-potential-independent anomalous charge density, and rotation-induced density corrections that reproduce exact field-theory results. Our framework provides a unified microscopic foundation for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics and establishes a direct link between quantum kinetic theory, spin polarization, magnetization, and anomalous transport.
authors: Gopal Mistry, Amaresh Jaiswal

papers.title: Genuinely Out-of-Equilibrium Bose-Einstein Condensation
papers.abstract: Bose-Einstein (BE) condensation typically occurs in the ground state. Prominent exceptions include excitons, whose ground state is the vacuum; consequently, they undergo BE condensation only in out-of-equilibrium regimes to counteract rapid decay. Here, we develop a driven-dissipative framework to address this challenge, demonstrating that BE condensates emerge under sufficiently strong excitation in one and two dimensions. In three dimensions, by incorporating effective loss rates and a specified injection energy, we find a percent-level condensate fraction, consistent in order of magnitude with the exciton experiment of Morita et al. (Nat. Commun. 13, 5388 (2022)).
authors: Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, Masahito Ueda

papers.title: The classical complexity of quantum state transmission
papers.abstract: Quantum communication provides a natural means to transmit quantum information, but how difficult is it to make such a transmission using only classical communication resources? We address this question by introducing classical communication models for quantum preparations and defining their minimum cost as the classical complexity. We prove that this complexity equals the amount of classical communication required to simulate quantum correlations in prepare-and-broadcast experiments, thus establishing a resource equivalence between quantum state transmission and quantum correlations. This calls for a general characterisation of the classical complexity of the noisy quantum state space, which we show grows exponentially with the quantum dimension and as a power-law in the inverse noise. It reveals the rapidly scaling fundamental cost of classical simulation. Moreover, we develop a toolbox of methods to certify classical complexity in quantum preparation devices, including an exact semidefinite-programming characterisation, analytical witnesses for symmetric preparations and convex programming scalable up to hundreds and sometimes thousands of qubit states. Our results establish classical complexity as a fundamental measure of quantum communication advantage, revealing the intrinsic cost of classically simulating quantum theory and providing practical tools for its certification.
authors: Elna Svegborn, Alexander Bernal, Armin Tavakoli

papers.title: Perturbation Algorithm and Iterative Realization of a Four-Layer Semi-Discrete Scheme for an Evolutionary Problem with a Variable Operator
papers.abstract: In a Hilbert space, we consider the Cauchy problem for an evolutionary equation with the operator $A+B(t)$, where $A$ is a self-adjoint positive definite operator and $B(t)$ is a bounded operator depending on time. By means of the perturbation algorithm, the purely implicit four-layer semi-discrete scheme of the third order of approximation (the three-step backward differentiation formula) is reduced to three two-layer schemes, whose solutions are used to construct an approximate solution of the original problem. In each two-layer scheme, the term containing $B(t)$ is moved to the right-hand side, and the resulting equation is solved by an iterative method, so that only the time-independent operator $I+\tau A$ has to be inverted; the convergence of the iterations at the rate of a geometric progression with a ratio of order $\tau$ is proved. A priori estimates for the two-layer and four-layer schemes are obtained by means of a discrete analogue of Gronwall's lemma. An estimate of order $\tau^3$ for the error of the approximate solution is proved under an assumption on the difference quotients of the computed grid functions on the first layers. The results are illustrated by numerical experiments.
authors: David Gulua, Jemal Rogava, Zurab Vashakidze

papers.title: Local-channel inequivalence within analytic symmetry-broken phases
papers.abstract: Gibbs states at different temperatures can be inequivalent under two-way quasi-local channels even within a single phase with spontaneously broken continuous symmetry and analytic free energy. We prove this for the symmetry-invariant Gibbs states of a canonical ideal Bose gas at fixed density and a classical vortex-free Villain model on hypercubic lattices in $d\ge3$ dimensions. At lower temperatures, two distant observers can estimate the shared direction of order more accurately. The maximum mutual information they can obtain by separate measurements grows logarithmically with the radius of their regions. The leading term is the same throughout each ordered phase, while the constant term $\mathcal{C}(T)=\tfrac12\ln[\Upsilon(T)/T]+c_{\mathrm{geom}}$ is strictly larger at lower temperatures. Here $\Upsilon(T)$ is the phase stiffness and $c_{\mathrm{geom}}$ depends only on the region geometry. A quasi-local channel cannot increase this constant, so it is invariant under two-way conversion. Cooling would increase it and is therefore impossible between any two distinct temperatures in the ordered phase. On finite lattices, cooling with vanishing error requires a circuit whose causal radius grows at least linearly with the lattice side length. We also obtain the invariant for quantum and multicomponent Villain models and conjecture a stiffness formula for more general patterns of continuous symmetry breaking.
authors: Guanxi Xun, Rintaro Masaoka, Weiguang Cao, Haruki Watanabe

papers.title: A receiver-side approach to confirm phase randomization in BB84 time-bin QKD with weak coherent pulses
papers.abstract: In quantum cryptography using time-bin BB84 protocols, the relative phase of symbol pulses has to be random to avoid vulnerability to coherent attacks. Typically this phase randomization is checked on the sender side. Here, we propose a protocol for monitoring and confirming phase randomization independently on the receiver side during operation. The proposed method can be implemented on the single-photon level without the need for any physical adaptation of the receiver. This can provide an additional tool for monitoring against possible eavesdropping attempts that affect the phase randomization.
authors: Bedir Halc{\i}, Rainer Kaltenbaek

papers.title: Chasing the KPZ exponents
papers.abstract: Forty years after it was written down, the Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation is the paradigm of scale invariance far from equilibrium. In one dimension it has been solved exactly and confirmed by precision experiments, and its scaling has now been observed in two-dimensional polariton condensates. Above one dimension, however, not a single exponent is known exactly, and even the existence of an upper critical dimension is disputed. In this Perspective we argue that firm statements need not wait for exact solutions. Treating the nonlinearity as an effective noise that acts on a fractal subset of the substrate leads to bounds on the roughness exponent, $1/(d+1)\le\alpha\le 1/d$ in $d$ dimensions. We examine the assumptions behind these bounds, confront them with four decades of theory, simulations and the new experiments, and identify the tests---foremost in three and more dimensions---that would establish or refute them.
authors: Luciano C. Lapas (Latin-American Institute of Life and Natural Sciences, Federal University for Latin-American Integration, Foz do Igua\c{c}u, Brazil), M\'arcio S. Gomes-Filho (International Center of Physics, Institute of Physics, University of Bras\'{\i}lia, Bras\'{\i}lia, Brazil), Fernando A. Oliveira (International Center of Physics, Institute of Physics, University of Bras\'{\i}lia, Bras\'{\i}lia, Brazil)

papers.title: Cardinal RG=GR: Phase-Space Cardinality and the Cosmological Constant and Hierarchy Problems
papers.abstract: The effective field theory approach constructs the low-energy theory by integrating out fluctuations above an ultraviolet scale which raises the cosmological constant and hierarchy problems. We investigate an alternative prescription in which the quantum theory is restricted to a finite accessible region of phase space, characterized by a dimensionless cardinality $\mathcal N$, rather than by independently prescribed spacetime and momentum scales. At fixed cardinality these scales are related. For Euclidean de Sitter space, the stationarity condition for the gravitational action can then be written as a stationarity condition with respect to the momentum scale, a relation which we call Cardinal RG=GR. We demonstrate the relation between $\mathcal N$ and the Gibbons-Hawking entropy of de Sitter space, compute the cosmological constant proportional to ${1}/{\sqrt{\mathcal N}}$, show that it is radiatively stable and apply the same prescription to demonstrate the radiative stability of the mass parameter for a simple interacting scalar field model, thereby illuminating the resolution of the hierarchy problem. We also establish a precise limit, involving gravitational data, in which the conventional results of Quantum Field Theory and the Renormalization Group are recovered.
authors: Laurent Freidel, Jerzy Kowalski-Glikman, Robert G. Leigh, Djordje Minic

papers.title: Ellis: Extremely Fast Quantum Circuit Simulation under Qubit Loss and Leakage
papers.abstract: Qubit loss and leakage are persistent errors: while a qubit remains lost or leaked, every operation acting on it is dropped. Consequently, the Clifford circuit executed differs from shot to shot. This variation breaks Pauli-frame simulation, which constructs each shot by XORing sampled Pauli flips onto a single \emph{common reference} measurement record. By rethinking the roles of tableau simulation and Pauli-frame simulation, we show that many key fault-tolerant primitives nevertheless retain a common reference under loss. These include CSS code memory, lattice surgery, and transversal CNOT. Such circuits can therefore be simulated exactly under Pauli noise and loss by a Pauli frame with per-shot masks for the dropped operations. We define \emph{frame-CSS} circuits as those that are CSS up to local single-qubit basis changes, given a loss model that specifies where qubits can be lost and reloaded. We prove that every frame-CSS circuit has a common reference, and we give a practically near-linear-time procedure that certifies whether a circuit is frame-CSS. We implement the certifier and a high-performance simulator in the open-source package \href{https://github.com/isaachyw/ELLIS}{\textsc{Ellis}} (Efficient Loss and Leakage Invariant-reference Simulation). On the gross code under qubit loss and Pauli errors, \ellis{} samples 952{,}000 shots per second on a single CPU core, at least $1000\times$ faster than Clifft~\cite{chase2026} and PPVM~\cite{luo2026ppvm}.
authors: Yuewen Hou, Gokul Subramanian Ravi

papers.title: Full-Color Two-loop Four-point Form Factor in N=4 SYM with Global CK-duality
papers.abstract: We determine the full-color two-loop four-point MHV form factor of the stress-tensor supermultiplet in N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory. Using color-kinematics (CK) duality and unitarity cuts, we construct complete one- and two-loop integrands manifesting global off-shell CK duality without explicit $\mu^2$ dependence. Integration-by-parts reduction to uniform-transcendentality master integrals yields purely rational numbers multiplying simple kinematic prefactors, manifesting maximal transcendentality. Expressing the form factor in terms of pentagon functions, we verify full-color infrared-pole cancellation, extract the finite remainder, and obtain new non-planar results for the two-loop triple-collinear splitting function and double-soft current.
authors: Zhiming Cai, Yuanhong Guo, Gang Yang

papers.title: The role of complementarity and quantum correlation in the uncertainty relations and the optimum states
papers.abstract: Uncertainty relations are used in quantum mechanics to illustrate the complementarity of two observables, assuming there is a lower bound for the product of their dispersions that depends on the first-order quantum correlation and the commutation relation of those observables in an optimum state. In this work, we demonstrate that the complex parameter of the optimum state equation has real and imaginary parts that depend on the first-order quantum correlation and the commutation relation between the observables in the optimum state, respectively. We apply our results to a two-level system, finding that the first-order quantum correlation and the commutation relation of two spin-1/2 projections in the optimum state complement each other and, finally, when the term correlation is used, a lower bound for the uncertainty principle does not depend on any parameter of the optimum state, in contrast to the usual form of the Heisenberg principle.
authors: Sttiwuer D\'iaz-Sol\'orzano, Goosline Alfredo Pereira Narv\'aez

papers.title: Notes on non-equilibrium thermodynamics of Robinson-Trautman spacetimes
papers.abstract: Robinson-Trautman spacetimes are determined by a parabolic heat-type evolution equation of fourth order for a scalar field on future null infinity. This equation may be re-written as an energy balance for an asymptotically time-like observer. In turn, it becomes a first law in the context of non-equilibrium thermodynamics if the non-linear memory is interpreted as heat. This leads to a local version of temperature and a manifestly increasing entropy density from the viewpoint of the environment.
authors: Glenn Barnich

papers.title: Improving the signal-to-noise ratio through postselection of coincident detections in anticounterfeiting and quantum key distribution
papers.abstract: In quantum communications and other photon-counting applications, reliably detecting weak optical signals against a strong noise background remains a fundamental challenge. In this paper, we develop a simple idea: when a signal is carried by pairs (or more generally multiplets) of photons emitted simultaneously, postselection of coincident detections recorded on two detectors makes it possible to improve-sometimes drastically-the Signal to Noise Ratio. Essentially, this is made possible by the fact that genuine and accidental coincidences scale differently with the width of the postselection window. As long as the window remains wide enough to retain detections from the same pair, the genuine coincidence rate is approximately unchanged. In contrast, coincidences formed from independent clicks decrease linearly as the window is narrowed. The resulting signal-to-noise ratio, therefore, increases inversely with the window width. Our approach makes it possible to reveal photon-pair signals that are otherwise hidden beneath a much stronger uncorrelated background. We analyze here applications of this idea to quantum key distribution, metrology, and anti-counterfeiting.
authors: Paula Wieteska-Bajak, Mohamed Hatifi, Renaud Mathevet, Vincent Lacombe, Jerome Wenger, Thomas Durt

papers.title: Cooperativity-enhanced single-photon emission in a topological quantum emitter chain
papers.abstract: Single-photon emitters are one of the key elements in state-of-the art quantum technologies, yet optimizing and manipulating their emission requires precise fabrication of the emitter systems themselves. Here, we propose a route to tailored single-photon emission by exploiting cooperative effects in a topological single-photon emitter chain. Although the involvement of multiple emitters normally suppresses single-photon emission, we show that localized topological edge modes restore single-photon emission and protect against local perturbations. At the same time, cooperative effects occur due to the collective nature of the edge modes, leading to directional emission and linewidth narrowing. Our findings open new possibilities for tailoring single-photon emission by combining cooperativity and topological effects.
authors: Jonathan Sturm, Irene Burghardt, Bert Hecht, Adriana P\'alffy

papers.title: To predict or to persist: how decoherence shapes learning in a spin-qubit quantum reservoir
papers.abstract: In this work we investigate how dephasing and the choice of measured observables affect learning in a simulated six-qubit spin chain with Markovian dissipation and exact expectation-value readout. For externally driven nonlinear autoregressive moving-average signals, combining single- and two-qubit observables gives better predictions than a population-only readout at comparable polynomial feature counts. Most of the configurations we tested become more accurate than a reference with relaxation and dephasing disabled, most strongly at $T_2=1\,\mu$s, where total memory capacity drops, and still at $T_2=5$-$10\,\mu$s, where memory is only redistributed across delays. For autonomous generation, we train the readout with scheduled sampling and iterative dataset aggregation to expose it to states reached under its own feedback. We do not find a clear systematic dependence of limit-cycle persistence on coherence across the reservoir ensemble. For chaotic forecasting, in contrast, prediction horizons at $T_2=1\,\mu$s shorten in all 10 reservoir realizations relative to that reference. For the noise-driven strange non-chaotic attractor, the model produces a smooth, approximately closed orbit, and neither captures the target's scatter nor follows its trajectory pointwise. We conclude that, within this simulated reservoir, the impact of coherence depends strongly on the task.
authors: Nikolaos Petropoulos, Elena Blokhina

papers.title: CAVQS: Context-Aware Variational Quantum Circuit Synthesis via Unitary Redistribution and Dynamic Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Variational quantum circuit synthesis jointly searches circuit structure and continuous parameters to reduce costly two-qubit gates, but block-based workflows typically instantiate blocks independently, limiting simplification across block boundaries. Moreover, fully unitary synthesis does not exploit opportunities created by permitted output measurements and classical feedforward. We present CAVQS, a context-aware variational synthesis framework that combines unitary redistribution and dynamic reconstruction. First, CAVQS uses QR decomposition to transfer unitary factors between overlapping blocks, preserving the overall transformation while reshaping local synthesis targets to enable cross-block reductions. Second, for blocks that precede permitted terminal measurements, CAVQS constructs ancilla-free dynamic implementations with a CNOT-budgeted pre-measurement search and analytic branch-unitary construction, thereby minimizing expected CNOT cost. Across random-circuit targets, CAVQS reduces mean two-qubit gate counts by 28.79%-42.52%, 2.05%-52.62%, and 30.51%-74.64% relative to QFAST, SQUANDER, and Fast-USYN, respectively, on common successful instances. On 4--6-qubit quantum algorithm benchmarks, the corresponding reductions are 27.27%-36.77%, 20.65%-69.10%, and 36.31%-71.88%, respectively.
authors: Zhilong Liu, Xiangzhen Zhou, Yunqi Huang, Xin Hong, Pengcheng Zhu, Fanxu Meng, Zhenlong Du

papers.title: A sensitivity-constrained polynomial method for DQC1 query complexity
papers.abstract: The polynomial method is one of the fundamental techniques for proving lower bounds on quantum query complexity, particularly in the BQP query model. In this work, we develop an analogue of the polynomial method for the DQC1 query model. We introduce the notion of {\em sensitivity approximate degree} for Boolean functions and show that it provides a lower bound on DQC1 query complexity. We establish several basic structural properties of this new measure. As a first result, we show that every nonconstant total Boolean function on $N$ input variables has sensitivity approximate degree $\Omega(N)$, and hence requires $\Omega(N)$ queries in the DQC1 model. Thus, unlike in the BQP query model, DQC1 admits no asymptotic query speedup for total Boolean functions. For symmetric partial Boolean functions, we give a complete characterization of the sensitivity approximate degree in terms of the separation between oppositely labeled Hamming weight layers. This yields a tight quadratic separation between sensitivity approximate degree and standard approximate degree, and also leads to tight quadratic separations between DQC1 and BQP query complexities. We further establish quantitative average-case classical simulation theorems for DQC1 algorithms. Finally, we apply our framework to Fourier analysis, obtaining a simple proof of an $\Omega(N^{1/4})$ DQC1 query lower bound for the 2-Forrelation problem.
authors: Changpeng Shao

papers.title: Flux-induced condensation in a radial geometry
papers.abstract: Stirring and shear usually suppress phase separation, but transport through a boundary can induce it. We study a binary mixture that is stable everywhere at rest and fills a two-dimensional annulus. The inner boundary is semipermeable and exchanges material with a permeate held at a fixed chemical potential, so that a steady flux of one component crosses the annulus. Although this driven system carries a steady current and produces entropy, within Model B dynamics its steady state is an equilibrium profile in an effective external field that is logarithmic in the distance from the center. Its strength is not imposed from outside but set by the permeate and the permeability of the boundary. Above a threshold driving flux, a condensed annulus forms around the inner boundary. It is bounded by a stationary front whose radius depends exponentially on the ratio of the bulk driving force to the flux. The front is pinned by the effective field and does not coarsen, and the threshold flux decreases only as the inverse logarithm of the system size. The driving flux shifts the phase lines but leaves the critical temperature unchanged. Interfacial tension gives rise to a critical nucleus and to a fold, at which the condensed state ceases to exist, with a threshold that we obtain in closed form. Numerical solutions confirm these predictions and reveal a hysteresis loop bounded by two saddle-node bifurcations. By symmetry, the theory also describes cavitation around a sink.
authors: Yoav Tsori

papers.title: Adaptive Hamiltonian Identification via Quantum Reinforcement Learning under Non-Stationary Dynamics
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of the Hamiltonian governing a quantum system is important for quantum-system characterization, device calibration, simulation, and reliable operation of quantum hardware. In practical systems, however, the governing dynamics may vary over time because of parameter drift, changing control conditions, or transitions between operating regimes. In this work, we formulate Hamiltonian identification as a quantum reinforcement learning (QRL) problem in which a quantum agent processes sequential quantum-state observations and estimates the governing Hamiltonian parameters. We first consider stationary dynamics using a Vanilla-QRL agent and then introduce a recurrent GRU-QRL architecture to track non-stationary dynamics. The framework is evaluated on transverse-field Ising model systems under stationary dynamics, abrupt Hamiltonian switching, rapidly changing Hamiltonians, random switch locations over longer trajectories, and gradual Hamiltonian drift. We further compare the proposed approach with a Quantum Graph Recurrent Neural Network (QGRNN) baseline and evaluate frozen policies on unseen trajectories. Results show that both approaches accurately reconstruct stationary Hamiltonians, while GRU-QRL provides substantially improved tracking under non-stationary dynamics. These results demonstrate the potential of recurrent QRL as an adaptive system-identification tool for monitoring time-varying quantum systems.
authors: Jawaher Kaldari, Saif Al-Kuwari

papers.title: Efficient calculation of the full Laguerre-Gaussian spectrum of entangled biphotons
papers.abstract: The spatial biphoton state generated by spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) enables applications in high-dimensional quantum information processing and is often described in Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) modes. However, calculating the full LG spectrum for arbitrary radial and orbital angular momentum (OAM) indices requires computationally demanding multidimensional integrations. We present a generating-function approach that analytically performs the four-dimensional transverse spatial integral without approximating the phase-matching function. The source geometry can be completely described by a few dimensionless parameters, which reduce to two parameters for wave-vector-degenerate photons with equal waists. Our derived expressions for the full LG spectrum allow for computationally efficient and numerically stable evaluation at high mode orders, addressing a crucial obstacle in previous works. To illustrate our approach, we compare OAM spectra obtained by projection onto the lowest radial order and by radially insensitive detection, and investigate how high-dimensional maximal entanglement can be approached by tuning source parameters. Our results provide a new analytical tool for efficiently characterizing and engineering high-dimensional spatial entanglement in SPDC.
authors: Jiabao Peng, Richard Bernecker, Stephan Fritzsche

papers.title: Fast extraction of universal data from temporal spectrum: Applications to Haagerup CFT and monopole scattering
papers.abstract: Extracting precise universal data on conformal field theory (CFT) on the lattice traditionally requires large-scale simulations of the ground states and excitations of critical systems. Here, we propose an alternative accurate and fast algorithm, where we read off the CFT spectrum from the transfer matrix spectrum of an infinite matrix product state after a short imaginary-time evolution. We apply this method to extract the charge-resolved spectrum of a Haagerup CFT to higher levels and obtain a central charge $c = 2.137(27)$. Moreover, we show that the Maldacena--Ludwig monopole boundary can be realized as the ground state of the Fidkowski--Kitaev Hamiltonian after space-time rotation.
authors: Tokiro Numasawa, Boris De Vos, Masataka Watanabe, Atsushi Ueda

papers.title: Wigner-Dyson correlations in selected sectors of an integrable spin chain
papers.abstract: In quantum many-body physics spectral statistics is often used as a probe to distinguish integrable and chaotic models. We find a special case of an integrable spin chain with unusual spectral properties. With open boundary conditions the model has homogeneous exponential degeneracies; these are split for periodic boundary conditions. In the latter case, we find that a small number of sectors (selected by a global symmetry) showcase Wigner-Dyson spectral statistics, which usually signals quantum chaos. Our model is clean, translationally invariant, and it fits into the standard Yang-Baxter framework. We identify Hilbert space fragmentation as the key mechanism behind the spectral properties. The fragmentation is non-local, and its extent is different in the case of open and periodic boundary conditions. We argue that the dynamics of the model is not chaotic despite the unusual spectral correlations.
authors: Bal\'azs Pozsgay

papers.title: Exact finite-time fluctuation-response relations for Markov processes: A martingale framework
papers.abstract: Fluctuations and responses of time-integrated observables are both experimentally measurable, and relations between them can reveal the dissipation that sustains a nonequilibrium state. Here we develop a martingale framework that gives exact finite-time fluctuation-response identities for additive observables of general Markov processes. We obtain an exact identity for the variance of an observable in terms of its Doob martingale, which splits the total variance into a part inherited from the initial ensemble and a part generated by noise during the observation. We show that, at fixed preparation, the response of the mean of the observable to any admissible perturbation is the covariance between the Doob martingale and a second martingale that represents the perturbation. For diffusions and jump processes, a single martingale amplitude determines both the fluctuations and the response of the observable. These identities yield inequalities, variational principles, and multivariate and frequency-domain bounds, whose costs are set by the corresponding physical perturbations. Applying the framework to underdamped dynamics, we obtain a friction-response thermodynamic uncertainty relation (TUR) that can be saturated at any finite time and thus gives a variational principle for the entropy production. We also demonstrate exponentially strong violations of the conventional TUR by velocity-resolved currents, even in linear Gaussian dynamics, and derive a weak-noise dissipation-coherence bound for limit cycles, which shows that inertial oscillators can beat the overdamped bound only if their frequency is weakly sensitive to friction. For overdamped dynamics and jump processes, the framework recovers and extends recent fluctuation-response identities and identifies when the corresponding uncertainty relations are saturated.
authors: Tan Van Vu, Van Tuan Vo, Ruicheng Bao, Keiji Saito

papers.title: Exact Spherical Branes and Deformations: BMN, IKKT and $\mathcal{N}=2^\ast$
papers.abstract: We present a unified analytic solution to the BPS equations of spherical Dp-branes for $1\leq p \leq 5$ and give the corresponding type II uplifts in closed form. These are holographically dual to maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory on $S^{p+1}$. The change of variables that makes the BPS equations integrable also allows us to analytically calculate a universal result for the holographic Wilson loop and obtain UV asymptotic behaviour previously determined numerically. The same change of variables extends naturally, with suitable modifications, to the cases $p=0$ and $p=-1$. We obtain a 1-parameter family of D0-brane solutions and show how the IR conditions lead to a singular limit of the integration constant. We also solve the D(-1)-brane BPS equations and show the resulting Euclidean uplift fails regularity conditions. Separately, we obtain an explicit representation of the one-ball electrostatic solution of polarised IKKT, which lets us express multipole moments and holographic observables using elliptic invariants. Finally, we analytically solve the BPS equations of the holographic dual of $\mathcal{N}=2^\ast$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory on $S^4$, present the corresponding type IIB uplift and calculate the holographic Wilson loop.
authors: Cameron Gibson

papers.title: All-Order Linearized Hydrodynamics of Charged Holographic Plasmas
papers.abstract: We investigate linearized all-order transport in a finite-density holographic plasma described by five-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory. By retaining the full frequency- and momentum-dependence of the fluid/gravity equations, we determine generalized shear, diffusion, higher-gradient, and chiral-vortical transport functions together with their real-time memory kernels. The different channels exhibit a clear hierarchy of temporal response: the leading shear and diffusion sectors respond promptly, whereas the higher-gradient sectors develop only after a finite buildup time. Remarkably, the chiral-vortical response also shows a finite buildup time despite entering at first order in the hydrodynamic derivative expansion, demonstrating that derivative order does not by itself determine the temporal organization of transport. Toward the near-extremal regime, long-time memory becomes increasingly persistent across several channels. These results reveal how finite density reshapes nonlocal transport and relaxation in strongly coupled holographic plasmas.
authors: Karthik R., Shamant Shreedhar Dixit, K. M. Ajith, Kartheek Hegde, Shreyas Punacha, A. Naveena Kumara

papers.title: Dynamical Temperley-Lieb algebras from Quiver CFTs
papers.abstract: The one-loop dilatation operator of a superconformal planar gauge theory can be written as a sum of local generators. The algebra these generators satisfy is a powerful organising principle for the spectrum. For SU(2)-like bosonic subsectors we show that this algebra can be read off directly from Feynman diagrams, which we identify as a natural graphical language for it. For N=4 super Yang-Mills this simply reproduces the Temperley-Lieb (TL) algebra of the XXX spin chain. After orbifolding and marginally deforming to N=2 superconformal quiver theories, the same recipe yields dynamical generalisations of the TL algebra. In these theories, the faces of the diagrams are coloured according to the quiver nodes, and separated by domain walls corresponding to bifundamental fields. There are two inequivalent SU(2)-like subsectors, which lead to two different TL algebras. One sector is built from the two bifundamental scalars and (in the simplest case) gives a dynamical TL algebra with a colour-dependent loop fugacity in its quadratic relation. The other sector is built from one bifundamental and one adjoint scalar, and (always) gives a novel algebra, in which the cubic TL relation becomes dynamical. In this latter case, we show that each generator of this new algebra is related to a standard XXZ TL generator by a colour-dependent twist. This twist is local and not an algebra homomorphism, and can be written as a dynamical Drinfeld twist. In both sectors, the TL structure provides a natural graphical approach to the spectral problem, as well as clarifying the structure of the irreducible representations of these chains. Finally, we give a preliminary description of the loop models associated to these algebras.
authors: Rob Klabbers, Elli Pomoni, Ana L. Retore, Paul Ryan, Konstantinos Zoubos

papers.title: Black holes and 2-group symmetry from blackfolds in minimal supergravity
papers.abstract: We investigate the black hole phase diagram of five-dimensional minimal supergravity using the blackfold approach and the framework of generalized symmetries. Starting from supergravity coupled to probe sources, we derive the 2-group (non-)conservation laws, construct the equilibrium action for a two-dimensional 2-group fluid, and compute the associated global conserved charges. We then match the thermodynamics of the general non-extremal black string in the ungauged theory to that of this fluid, organizing the blackfold effective theory and its solutions in terms of symmetry invariants. In the non-extremal ungauged sector, we perturbatively construct new black rings, Saturns, di-rings, and bi-rings, including a black Saturn with seven independent parameters. Taking appropriate extremal limits, we identify several extremal branches, some previously unexplored and others anticipated, as well as BPS branches that approximate known supersymmetric families. Finally, we apply the same framework to construct extremal black rings in AdS$_5$, identifying three regular branches that are promising candidates for an exact completion.
authors: Jay Armas, Giorgos Batzios, Pedro Vicente Marto, Chiara Toldo

papers.title: A Tensor-Algebraic No-Go Theorem for High-Dimensional Photonic Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger States Discovered with AlphaProof Nexus
papers.abstract: Photonic GHZ states generated with probabilistic pair sources can be described by edge-coloured, complex-weighted graphs. In this representation, conditioning on an event with one photon in every detector turns the output amplitudes into coherent sums over perfect matchings, and generating an \(N\)-photon \(D\)-dimensional GHZ state is equivalent to constructing a monochromatic quantum graph. Here, we prove that no complex-weighted monochromatic quantum graph exists for any even \(N\ge4\) when \(D\ge N\). The proof, discovered through AI-assisted formal proof search in Lean using AlphaProof Nexus, constructs a weighted sum \(\mathcal F\) of amplitudes whose coefficients factor vertex by vertex. Summing over the colours at one fixed vertex reduces the problem to an \((N-1)\times N\) matrix of effective edge weights. For the graph amplitudes \(\omega\) and GHZ target \(\Delta\), the row--column imbalance yields \(\mathcal F(\omega)=0\) but \(\mathcal F(\Delta)\neq0\), contradicting the required equality \(\omega=\Delta\). Finally, we give a physical interpretation of the AI-discovered mathematical proof.
authors: Mario Krenn, Moritz Firsching, George Tsoukalas, Rishikesh Gajjala, Xuemei Gu, Swarat Chaudhuri

papers.title: All Non-Contextual Pauli Hamiltonians are Free-Fermion in Disguise
papers.abstract: Decomposing Hamiltonians into classically tractable fragments is central to quantum simulation. One such way of doing so is the contextual subspace decomposition, which expresses the Hamiltonian with respect to non-contextual sets of Paulis. The conditions for contextuality rely on the anticommutation and commutation of Pauli operators; it is therefore natural to make an explicit connection between non-contextuality and fermionic physics. Theoretical work is centered around two theorems: in the first, we consider non-contextual Pauli Hamiltonians and show that they are free-fermion-disguised. In the second we write these Pauli non-contextual Hamiltonians in terms of Majorana and Dirac fermionic operators, showing that they carry a Jordan--Wigner-like fermion-to-qubit encoding. These two central theorems are formalized in the proof assistant language Lean. We use this to describe the space of fermionic non-contextual Hamiltonians, and highlight their relation to the more general class of free-fermion-disguised Hamiltonians. We further develop a heuristic algorithm to find line-graph based free-fermion fragments and their connected components of molecular Hamiltonians. We benchmark our algorithms against non-contextual searches for encoded molecular Hamiltonians and find comparable performance in identifying free-fermion solvable components. Our work has implications for what fragments to consider as useful for quantum simulation.
authors: Andrew M. Projansky, Weishi Wang, Kevin A. Reiss, James D. Whitfield

papers.title: Stitching Quantum Codes into Quilts: Universal Logic with no Ancillary Qubits
papers.abstract: Proposals abound for performing fault-tolerant logical Pauli-product measurements between quantum codes beyond the surface code. We introduce a new construction, the code quilt, whereby a target joint logical operator of two or more codeblocks is directly measured without the use of an ancillary system. We construct explicit circuits to perform a logical measurement using the quilt construction, which also require no physical qubits beyond the ancillas already in place to perform idle syndrome extraction on the codeblocks in question. We give a detailed structural analysis of the construction, which is based on a subsystem code, and provide several sets of sufficient conditions under which the relevant code-capacity distance is preserved. We give two variants of the protocol. The first, where the gauge generators of the subsystem code are measured directly, is provably not fault tolerant in the large-distance limit but admits a particularly practical circuit implementation in which the physical qubit degree increases by at most two. The second has more favourable asymptotic properties, although we do not prove its fault tolerance in the general case. We then perform an extensive empirical analysis of the technique, in particular of the first variant, as applied to bivariate bicycle and surface codes, finding code-capacity-distance preserving quilts for measuring 25,000 randomly selected logical operators. We optimise to find sparse and decongested detector bases for each and, for a randomly selected subset, find circuits that we estimate to be distance preserving. Finally, we perform decoding experiments on a subset of these circuits and find that their logical error probability is comparable to that of idle memory for operations involving the 144-qubit bivariate bicycle code and distance-12 rotated surface code at physical error rates between $1.5\times 10^{-3}$ and $3\times 10^{-3}$.
authors: Stasiu Wolanski

papers.title: Quantifying the irrealism required by quantum random access codes
papers.abstract: How far must decoding observables be from having elements of reality to achieve a given quantum advantage in a communication task? We answer this question for quantum random access codes. Here, an observable has an element of reality when its unrevealed measurement leaves the preparation undisturbed; its irrealism is the relative entropy to the closest such preparation. Because it comprises local coherence and the correlations destroyed by the unrevealed measurement, irrealism applies to prepare-and-measure (PM) and entanglement-assisted (EA) codes alike. For PM codes decoded in mutually unbiased bases, we obtain the irrealism frontier, the least total irrealism compatible with each success probability, exactly in every dimension; an excess-irrealism identity shows that Gibbs states of the decoding operator attain it uniquely. For PM codes minimized also over the decoders, the required irrealism vanishes up to the classical value and is positive beyond it; for qubits, mutually unbiased decoders are not the cheapest below a success probability of 0.833. For EA codes with a qubit receiver, trusted decoders, and parity-dependent sender settings, the frontier exceeds the PM one by the realism-based nonlocality of the contexts used by an optimal code, and with rank-one projective sender measurements a success probability above 0.815 certifies a minimum realism-based nonlocality of the shared state.
authors: Pedro R. Dieguez

papers.title: Analyticity of $\operatorname{Sine}_\beta$ pair correlations
papers.abstract: We prove that the pair correlation function of $\operatorname{Sine}_\beta$ extends holomorphically in $\beta$ to $\Re\beta>0$ at every fixed nonzero separation. Our proof combines a random walk representation of the stochastic sine phase moments, stretched-exponential Fourier decay obtained by coupling, and weighted energy estimates for complex $\beta$.
authors: Yun Li, Yahui Qu, Benedek Valk\'o, B\'alint Vir\'ag

papers.title: First-passage and correlated reset-count statistics under threshold and Poissonian resetting in a two-dimensional wedge geometry
papers.abstract: We study the interplay between threshold resetting (TR) and Poissonian resetting in a Brownian target search problem confined to a two-dimensional open wedge of apex angle $\alpha$. The boundary at zero angle acts as an absorbing target, while encounters with the boundary at $\alpha$ trigger TR, instantaneously restarting the search from its initial position. For TR alone, using the renewal framework developed by Biswas et al. in Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 227101 (2025), we obtain exact first and second moments of the first-passage time (FPT), whose density exhibits an algebraic long-time tail $t^{-1-\frac{\pi}{2\alpha}}$. To combine the two resetting mechanisms, we thereafter develop a generic random-variable-based renewal formalism to derive the combined mean FPT. We show that the coefficient of variation of the underlying TR dynamics determines whether Poissonian resetting accelerates or hinders the search for $0<\alpha<\pi/4$, whereas for $\alpha\geq\pi/4$, Poissonian resetting always reduces the MFPT. Furthermore, we derive the joint count statistics of the two resetting mechanisms and characterize their mutual dependence through Pearson's correlation coefficient. Interestingly, we uncover a crossover from weak to strong correlations as the Poissonian resetting rate is varied, with the crossover behavior exhibiting a nontrivial dependence on the initial search position. Our framework provides a basis for studying competing resetting mechanisms in more general geometries.
authors: Fazil Najeeb, Arnab Pal, V. V Prasad

papers.title: Elliptic analogues of KP and BKP hierarchies and their tau functions
papers.abstract: We develop a tau-function framework for soliton solutions on elliptic backgrounds associated with the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili (KP) hierarchy and its B-type counterpart (BKP). Starting from discrete KP (dKP) and discrete BKP (dBKP) equations of elliptic type, we construct Casorati and Gram determinant tau functions for the elliptic dKP through Darboux and binary Darboux transformations, and elliptic Pfaffian tau functions for dBKP through the Moutard transformation. Moreover, the higher-order discrete KP and BKP hierarchies together with their tau functions are constructed via Pfaffian identities. Then, through Miwa transformations, the continuous elliptic KP, modified KP, and BKP hierarchies and their tau functions are provided. Suitable constraints on spectral parameters or wave numbers yield reductions to the Korteweg--de Vries (KdV), focusing and defocusing modified Korteweg--de Vries (mKdV), and Sawada--Kotera (SK) equations, together with their solutions on elliptic backgrounds. We also construct KP line-soliton solutions and obtain lump solutions for the KP-I equation. For selected determinant families, we establish sufficient conditions for real-valuedness and global nonsingularity. The resulting framework provides a common approach to elliptic tau functions, their discrete and continuous bilinear identities, and the construction of solutions through reductions.
authors: Changyan Shi, Bao-Feng Feng

papers.title: Weyl-induced ultrasoft renormalization of the static QCD potential
papers.abstract:
We derive the leading curvature-dependent ultrasoft anomalous dimension of the static color-singlet potential in potential nonrelativistic QCD. In a Ricci-flat background the electric Weyl tensor introduces a $t^{-2}$ term in the short-time chromoelectric correlator. The resulting dipole self-energy is ultraviolet divergent at order $\alpha_s^2$ in the curvature sector, two orders earlier than the flat-space contribution. For $W=C_{\mu\alpha
u eta}r^\mu u^\alpha r^
u u^ eta$ and $V_s^{(W)}=c_W W/r$, we obtain $
u\,\partial_
u c_W=C_F C_A\alpha_s^2/(3\pi)$. We calculate the compensating soft infrared pole and the finite one-loop matching coefficient in an optical dimensional subtraction scheme. A direct physical-metric fermion calculation reproduces the finite light-flavor term. We also exhibit the cancellation of the leading regulated infrared overlap and the compensating transformation of soft and ultrasoft constants under an evanescent curvature rescaling. In the perturbative adiabatic regime the anomalous dimension fixes the coefficient of a curvature-dependent $\alpha_s^2\ln\alpha_s$ term in the static energy.
authors: Michael Wilson

papers.title: Quantum Autoencoder on Real Hardware for New Physics Searches at Muon Colliders
papers.abstract: We apply a quantum autoencoder to search for new physics (NP) in the tri-photon process $\mu^+\mu^-\to\gamma\gamma\gamma$ at muon colliders. Using a six-qubit circuit on the Tianyan176 quantum computer, we measure the reconstruction losses for Standard Model (SM) events and anomalous quartic gauge couplings (aQGCs) events. The results demonstrate that the hardware-implemented quantum autoencoder effectively discriminates NP signals from the SM background. Concurrently, we derive the expected constraints on the aQGCs coefficients and compare them with those obtained from conventional methods.
authors: Shuai Zhang, Ji-Chong Yang

papers.title: Entanglement, records, and quantum recovery in qubit chains
papers.abstract: We investigate entanglement, readable records and quantum recovery using an exactly solvable chain of sequentially interacting qubits. For weak interactions, entanglement reaches a later environment site before that site carries an equally strong local record. The leading local record is encoded in an off-diagonal element of the reduced density matrix and can be detected by a Pauli measurement, while a population measurement gives a higher-order signal. We further characterize the accessibility of the relative phase through joint transverse correlations and derive the optimal fidelity for recovering an unknown quantum state from the system and an accessible environment fragment. We show that interactions acting only within the environment can redistribute readable records and change the region required for quantum recovery without affecting the reduced state of the system.
authors: Sugumi Kanno, Jiro Soda

papers.title: Quantum Zeno Effect with a Superposed Measurement Schedule in Relational Time
papers.abstract: Motivated by the Page-Wootters construction in which time is a quantum clock reading and the global system state is stationary, we propose a quantum circuit that explores the observable consequences of treating measurement timing as a quantum degree of freedom. We place two Zeno measurement schedules of a driven qubit in a coherent superposition using a schedule qubit. We show that, for a fixed drive strength, the interference visibility between the two schedules depends only on the time offset between them, not on the number of intermediate measurements taken. Then we show that, for one schedule-readout outcome, the Zeno trend reverses, predicting a result that complements the standard Zeno probability. We propose a circuit implementation with physical memory qubits and show that measuring the memory register's joint $X$-basis parity distinguishes a coherent schedule from a classical or dephased one. We give the gate count and an error budget for a superconducting-qubit implementation. The Page-Wootters picture motivates this protocol and provides an equivalent stationary representation, although the predictions follow from the standard circuit description without requiring a relational-time interpretation. This is consistent with the Page-Wootters framework recovering standard quantum dynamics through correlations between a clock and the rest of the system.
authors: Olivia Seidel, Chiara Marletto, Jonathan Asaadi, Sara Sussman, Sayan Biswas, Vlatko Vedral

papers.title: Effect of coupling asymmetry on the spontaneous decay and entanglement of two atoms in a common cavity
papers.abstract: We investigate the dynamics and the spontaneous decay of two identical two-level atoms into the vacuum in a cavity at low temperature. We analytically derive the survival probability and the amplitudes of the state of the system by calculating the exact self-energy when the atoms are both initially excited. It is found that moderate asymmetry enhances the decay of the survival probability and increases the entanglement production in either lossless and lossy cavities.
authors: Yamen Hamdouni

papers.title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
papers.abstract: We establish a framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms, surpassing standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. Our three conjectures are as follows: 1. For fixed field content and derivative order, effective couplings form a finite-dimensional space under stated equivalences. 2. A family of mixed RR, gauge, and scalar interactions exists at all orders, represented by a finite number of effective even forms. 3. The higher-derivative contact-term sector can be constructed from a finite set of basic tensor structures using polynomials in derivative symbols. We introduce a higher-class pullback operator \( P_{\infty} \) and mixed transgression operators \( \mathcal{T}_{\infty} \), emphasizing amplitude-derived pole residues and local contact terms as key physical data. This formalism distinguishes admissible tensor structures, presenting characteristic-form aspects as conjectures alongside their validity considerations.
authors: Armin Hatefi, Ehsan Hatefi

papers.title: Root-of-Unity Limits of Trigonometric qKZ Connections
papers.abstract: Over the field of complex numbers, we study root-of-unity limits of trigonometric qKZ connections associated with tensor products of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ Verma modules and of their hypergeometric solutions. As the multiplicative step approaches a primitive $m$-th root of unity and the quantum-group and twist parameters approach $1$, the $m$-step qKZ transport yields, on every fixed-degree subspace,a differential connection. We show that this connection is the pullback of the trigonometric KZ connection under the power map $z\mapsto z^m$, with the KZ parameter rescaled by $m$, and establish formal and $\ell$-adic versions. In degree one, with all highest weights equal to $1$, we determine the limits of normalized qKZ hypergeometric circle integrals in arbitrary angular chambers. The limits are expressed in terms of loaded hypergeometric integrals for the trigonometric KZ equations and explicit chamber-dependent upper-triangular matrices. We establish compatibility of the resulting distinguished fundamental matrices under inward analytic continuation, governed by the right weak Bruhat order,and under power maps, including composition of root orders.
authors: Alexander Varchenko

papers.title: Twinor Theory in the Newton--Hooke Limit: A Nonrelativistic Schr\"odinger Equation for Arbitrary Spin
papers.abstract: The Newton--Hooke limit of the massive twinor field equations is derived at fixed particle mass and fixed cosmological acceleration per unit displacement. On a static torsion-free background, removal of the rest energy separates the leading spin amplitude from a finite sequence of auxiliary spinors. For every positive integer rank $2s$, a regular limit of exact solutions satisfies a first-order hierarchy. Its lowest two equations give a necessary Schr\"odinger equation for the leading amplitude, with a curvature term from the ordered spatial derivatives and a source determined by two projections of the relativistic source. The higher equations impose additional conditions. On the homogeneous Newton--Hooke background with trivial internal connection and nonzero cosmological acceleration parameter, vanishing of all limiting contracted sources forces the leading amplitude to vanish for $s\geq\tfrac32$. A separate reduction of the scalar wave equation gives the spin-zero case.
authors: Chen-Hsu Chien

papers.title: Imaginary-Time Density Correlations Encode Quantum Entropy and Free Energy
papers.abstract: In the classical limit, maximum-entropy inference yields an estimate of the excess entropy from the static structure factor through a single momentum sum. Quantum mechanically this estimate fails, because interactions also change the kinetic energy, while delocalization and exchange add information that equal-time correlations do not contain. We show that imaginary-time density correlations contain this information, and that with them the classical relation carries over to quantum systems. Such correlations are available from path-integral simulations and X-ray Thomson scattering. Relative-entropy inference over imaginary-time paths, with an ideal Bose or Fermi gas as reference, gives closed forms for the excess entropy and free energies, within the same Gaussian approximation as the classical relation. They recover the classical result and estimate entropy that the classical relation misses. We test them on weakly interacting bosons, interacting fermions on a ring, and the warm dense electron gas. The closed forms need only imaginary-time density correlations and their ideal-gas reference at a single state point, without using the interaction potential. Our approach can extend other classical entropy estimators to quantum systems.
authors: Sagi Meir

papers.title: Efficient Classical Algorithms for Ground Energy Estimation of Fermions with Conjugate-Pair Orbital Interactions
papers.abstract: Estimating the ground energy of interacting fermions is central to quantum many-body physics, and recent quantum algorithms provide polynomial-time guarantees for some structured families. Classical approaches commonly rely on quantum Monte Carlo, where the sign problem is a major obstacle. However, even when a nonnegative expansion without sign problem is available, rigorous guarantees for rapid mixing are still far from well understood. In this paper, we give an efficient classical randomized algorithm for approximating the ground energy of fermionic Hamiltonians with conjugate hopping matrices and conjugate-paired orbital interactions, which includes the attractive Hubbard models. This guarantee not only holds without a physical spectral gap or a weak-coupling assumption, but also covers interactions beyond onsite density attractions. Technically, we first reduce ground-energy estimation to partition-function estimation and then use a discretization with controlled energy error to obtain a nonnegative weighted sum of squared determinant moduli and then apply the Chen--Liu log-concave counting theorem. In addition, we obtain a sharper arithmetic bound by controlling how many independent sampling runs and matrix updates are needed, and using sparse matrices to reduce the cost of each update.
authors: Ziyi Yang, Yexin Zhang, Yuexin Su, Xinzhao Wang, Xiaoyang Wang, Tongyang Li

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Statistical Mechanics: Physical Concepts & Mathematical Tools
papers.abstract: As anything not in equilibrium is, by definition, nonequilibrium, there is no universally agreed-upon set of topics that can constitute an exhaustive presentation of nonequilibrium statistical mechanics. At the same time, nonequilibrium statistical mechanics has transcended traditional physics to become a powerful language for complex systems. Prompted by an enthusiastic curiosity about complex systems, these cursory lecture notes attempt to elucidate some introductory concepts and techniques used in classical nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, which find successful applications not only in foundational physics, but also across other fields such as biology, ecology, economics, and sociology. Except for the specific synthesis and presentation of the material, which assumes basic familiarity with equilibrium statistical mechanics, the author claims no originality.
authors: Sagar Chakraborty

papers.title: Non-Binary Detector Error Models
papers.abstract: A key challenge in fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) is that the syndrome extraction circuits are themselves faulty. Such circuit-level noise is commonly described by a detector error model (DEM). In Stim and in almost all related works, DEMs are binary: every non-binary circuit error (e.g., CNOT gate), is decomposed into independent binary error mechanisms. In this work, we introduce non-binary DEMs, in which each fault location of the syndrome extraction circuit is modeled by one random variable over its original alphabet, e.g., the 16 two-qubit Pauli errors after a CNOT gate. We also propose a split-merge-regroup transformation that builds a compact non-binary DEM from any Clifford circuit by merging the error components that flip the same detectors and observables. Non-binary DEMs represent any Pauli channel exactly, whereas binary DEMs are exact only for channels that factorize into independent binary parts. When the channels factorize, we prove that binary and non-binary DEMs are equivalent under degenerate quantum maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) decoding, but not under quantum MAP decoding. Although the variables are non-binary, belief propagation (BP) still exchanges a single scalar message per edge. Our numerical results with surface, color and bivariate bicycle codes show that non-binary DEMs have two main advantages. First, their Tanner graphs have four to five times fewer edges, which is advantageous for hardware implementations. Second, their performance under BP, with and without OSD post-processing, is better than that of their binary counterparts, and BP with OSD runs up to $9.4\times$ faster in a CPU.
authors: Stefano Tinelli, Francisco L\'azaro, Francisco Garc\'ia Herrero

papers.title: Curvature Integrability in Twinor Theory: An Ambitwistor Approach to the Twinor Googly Problem
papers.abstract: The twinor analogue of the googly problem is addressed through an ambitwistor structure defined by null autoparallels, retaining both chiralities, sources and torsion without requiring chiral null surfaces. Under the stated quotient, evaluation and descent assumptions, holomorphic affine sections reconstruct the twinor field equation $DY=J$. Correspondence-space cohomology realizes the contracted chiral and ladder equations, including the ladder's soldering coupling and mass-normalization source. For a prescribed non-normal conformal connection, infinity-twistor parallelism recovers the energy--momentum equation, supplemented by independent spin-current equations. These constructions give a conditional auxiliary formulation; constitutive sources and gravitational prescriptions remain dynamical input.
authors: Chen-Hsu Chien

papers.title: Aggregating soft-photon recoil with a positive finite-step sampler
papers.abstract: We model stochastic radiation reaction by aggregating soft photons into one positive recoil, retaining the local no-emission probability and two loss moments of the crossed-field QED kernel. Unlike Gaussian diffusion, the sampler preserves one-sided energy loss. Analytical synchrotron moments expose a finite-step cooling bias, which state feedback reduces. Laser and ion-channel tests probe excessive-loss risk and directed radiation spectra, providing a practical route to stochastic particle simulations without resolving individual soft emissions.
authors: Nina Elkina, Alexander Pukhov

papers.title: Half-strings across the deconfinement transition of a $U(1)$ quantum link model
papers.abstract: The phenomenon of confinement is arguably the key feature of gauge theories regularly studied in high-energy and condensed matter physics. This causes hadrons to exist as stable particles in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) as bound states of quarks (and gluons), and strings in pure gauge theories. The promise of realizing such strings in quantum simulator setups have fueled extensive studies of a plethora of simpler lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Quantum link models (QLMs) generalize Wilsonian LGTs and yield richer scenarios of confinement. For example, the string joining two static charges in the spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ $U(1)$ QLM fractionalize, giving rise to confining phases that break the point group and internal symmetries spontaneously. It was further shown in PRL 130, 071901 (2023) that adding annealed $Q = \pm 2$ charges to this model qualitatively changes the confinement-deconfinement transition. In this paper, we examine the finite temperature phase transition both in the presence and the absence of annealed charges through detailed extraction of critical temperature, $T_c$ , and exponents. The (effective) string tension $\sigma$ at zero and finite- temperatures are compared between the theory with and without annealed charges. The quantity $T_c/\sqrt{\sigma}$ for the QLM with annealed charges is similar to the usual $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory, while the theory without the charges provides a new universal value.
authors: Indrajit Sau, Arnab Sen, Debasish Banerjee

papers.title: Thermal Resummation Effects on Electroweak Phase Transitions and Gravitational Waves in Conformal and Non-Conformal 2HDMs
papers.abstract: We quantify how thermal resummation affects electroweak phase transitions and gravitational-wave predictions in classically conformal and non-conformal two-Higgs-doublet models. We compare multi-field partial dressing (PD), which retains the full thermal functions and determines scalar masses and mixing from gap equations, with the Parwani and Arnold-Espinosa (AE) prescriptions at identical zero-temperature inputs. Completed first-order transitions dominate the conformal scan under all three prescriptions. PD typically gives the strongest and most supercooled transitions, reaching $T_p/T_c \simeq 0.5$ versus $T_p/T_c \gtrsim 0.8$ for Parwani and AE. At every conformal point where all three predict completion, PD gives the largest gravitational-wave peak amplitude, followed by Parwani and AE. The non-conformal model has no universal ordering, and the prescription changes the type of thermal history across extended regions of parameter space. For representative benchmarks, PD and AE differ by up to about nine orders of magnitude in peak amplitude and a factor of about fifty in peak frequency. In multi-field PD, the dressed tadpole is not a gradient, so the reconstructed potential depends on the integration path. In benchmark tests, changing the path shifts the transition temperatures by at most about 7% and the peak amplitude by up to a factor of about three. This intrinsic ambiguity is smaller than the largest differences between prescriptions. Thermal resummation is a major source of uncertainty in these phase-transition and gravitational-wave predictions.
authors: Yu-Bo Zhao, Ji-Wei Li, Zhi-Wei Wang

papers.title: Tunable Ground-State Entanglement in Fully Connected Quantum Systems: From Logarithmic to Volume-Law Scaling
papers.abstract: Entanglement scaling is a central probe of the complexity of quantum many-body ground states, yet once geometric locality is absent, it can depend sensitively on the structure and normalization of interactions. For fully connected Hamiltonians with the natural Kac normalization, nondegenerate gapped ground states are known to obey a logarithmic entanglement bound. Here we ask how the ground-state entanglement changes when this interaction normalization is continuously relaxed away from the Kac scale. We answer this question by constructing an explicit all-to-all bipartite Hamiltonian of $n$ qubits with Fourier pairing amplitudes and pairwise interaction strength proportional to $n^{-\kappa}$. For sufficiently small fixed coupling, we prove that every pure ground state has entanglement entropy $\Theta(n^{2-2\kappa} \log n)$ for $1/2<\kappa\leq1$ and $\Theta(n)$ at $\kappa=1/2$. We further show that the ground state is unique and separated from the rest of the spectrum by a system-size-independent gap for $3/4 \leq \kappa \leq 1$, while weak-coupling analysis and numerical calculations suggest that the gap remains open also for $1/2 \leq \kappa < 3/4$. Thus, varying only the interaction normalization yields a controlled hierarchy from logarithmic scaling at the natural Kac normalization $\kappa=1$ to increasingly strong subextensive entanglement and ultimately to a volume law, showing that even an arbitrarily weak relaxation of this normalization precludes a universal logarithmic entanglement bound.
authors: Donghoon Kim, Tomotaka Kuwahara

papers.title: When lies look like noise: certifying untrusted entanglement swapping
papers.abstract: Entanglement swapping lets quantum repeaters distribute entanglement over long distances, a prerequisite for the quantum internet. We study its security in a noisy network whose intermediate nodes perform the quantum operations faithfully but may misreport the classical outcome that end users rely on. We show that the ideal functionality of entanglement swapping cannot be realised, because it gives the adversary no influence over the delivered state, whereas a node that relabels its report does have such influence. Including honest noise in the ideal setting does not help unless it also concedes a bounded fraction of misreported pairs. We therefore propose a cut-and-choose protocol that tests a random subset of pairs to certify the rest. Since no test can distinguish a misreport from readout noise, the protocol certifies the error above a pre-agreed minimum noise level, which is the misreport rate under our threat model. This yields a quality-of-service guarantee, in which a failure witnesses that the node did not deliver as agreed. Unlike verification schemes that consume the state they certify, the untested pairs remain available for use, with a finite-size guarantee. Certifying a 1% misreport rate on 10^6 pairs costs 10^4 to 1.7x10^5 test pairs, for minimum noise levels ranging from 0 to 5%. The main cost is memory, since 1% requires holding 10^5 to 10^6 pairs at once, far beyond the capacity of today's quantum memories. Verifying and releasing in blocks ties the memory to the block size at the cost of a weaker rate: a (10^4)-qubit memory certifies 14% on 4.7x10^5 delivered pairs.
authors: Maria Gragera Garces, Chris Heunen, Mahesh K. Marina

papers.title: Review of Pion and Nucleon Gluon Parton Distribution Functions from Lattice QCD
papers.abstract: Gluons play an essential role in the strong interaction that binds quarks into hadrons, as described by quantum chromodynamics (QCD). Understanding how the fundamental dynamics of QCD give rise to hadron structure remains one of the outstanding challenges in nuclear and particle physics. Parton distribution functions (PDFs) provide a successful framework for describing high-energy scattering processes involving hadrons. However, our knowledge of gluon PDFs remains comparatively limited because of the experimental challenges associated with directly constraining the gluon structure of hadrons. In recent years, a major breakthrough has enabled the calculation of the Bjorken-$x$ dependence of PDFs directly from lattice QCD. Among the available approaches, the large-momentum effective theory (LaMET) and pseudo-PDF frameworks have emerged as the most widely used methods and have produced the majority of lattice determinations of parton distributions. These developments have sparked rapid progress in first-principles studies of the $x$-dependent structure of hadrons, including gluon PDFs of the nucleon and pseudoscalar mesons. In this review, we summarize recent advances in lattice QCD calculations of gluon PDFs {using the LaMET and pseudo-PDF methods}, discuss the current status and impacts of these developments, and highlight the remaining challenges and future opportunities.
authors: William Good, Huey-Wen Lin

papers.title: Scaling classical hardware for accurate real-time quantum error correction
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires a classical decoder fast enough to process syndrome measurements at the rate at which they are generated, and to return its decisions with low latency. This is most demanding for superconducting processors, whose fast syndrome cycles force a trade-off between decoding speed and accuracy. Decoders fast enough to keep up sacrifice accuracy, which must be compensated for with larger codes and thus additional physical qubits. Here we introduce Rapids, a streaming neural decoder that is both fast and accurate. We achieve this by co-designing the decoder with a field-programmable gate array (FPGA): the network is built from operations that map cheaply onto the device and trained in its integer arithmetic. For the distance-19 surface code, Rapids decodes each round of syndromes in under a microsecond on a single FPGA, fast enough for superconducting processors, and returns its decisions with the low latency that fault-tolerant algorithms require. Its logical error rate is 240 times lower than that of existing real-time hardware decoders. The same design extends to the color code and the [[144,12,12]] bivariate-bicycle code, on which our decoder is 16 times more accurate than the real-time Relay decoder. We further show that the decoder scales: spread over several FPGAs or hardened into custom silicon, it becomes faster, more accurate, or able to decode larger codes. Classical hardware thus becomes a further resource, alongside qubits, that can be scaled to improve fault-tolerant quantum computers.
authors: Chenyang Jin, Susanne F. Yelin, Andi Gu

papers.title: Generic arm separation for planar percolation models
papers.abstract: Arm separation is an important technical tool in the study of critical and near-critical planar percolation systems. When combined with RSW estimates, it proves quasi-multiplicativity of arm-event probabilities, links the derivatives of different events and allows the identification of universal arm exponents. We provide a very generic statement of arm separation that applies to arbitrary planar percolation models. Our argument is based on exploring configurations conditioned on the existence of arms in such a way that "exposed" arms are revealed with positive probability. The exploration algorithm is independent of the percolation model and applies to all polychromatic arm events. As an application, we prove a strong arm-separation result for critical planar FK-percolation.
authors: Lo\"ic Gassmann, Ioan Manolescu, Maran Mohanarangan

papers.title: Global existence versus blow-up for Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou lattices
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the global behavior of infinite nonlinear lattices. In particular, for the Fermi--Pasta--Ulam--Tsingou-$\alpha$ lattice (FPUT-$\alpha$), we show global existence for small initial data via a region-based approach, and prove blow-up for negative energy and some positive energy, given appropriate conditions on the initial momentum and dispersion. Moreover, we extend these results to the nonlinear Klein-Gordon (DNKG) equation and nonlinear wave (DNW) equation. \
authors: Gerald Teschl, Anton Zand

papers.title: Bianchi cosmologies with four-dimensional groups of motion in New General Relativity
